# Wave 6 plan — CipherBox v2

Planned 2026-08-06 against `main` @ `a798ebf4e` (all 7 wave-5 PRs merged, tree green in both
languages: Rust 1493 tests, TS typecheck/lint/test/tracker-refs all 0).

## The strategic frame — this wave is different

Waves 1–5 were engine-and-web interior work. **Wave 6 is the first wave where the deploy critical
path is reachable**, because #648 became startable today.

```
648 → 649 → 650 → 651 → 653 (staging cutover) → 656 (Grafana)
                     ↑              ↑           └→ 652 (nightly tier)
642 ────→ 643 ───────┘              │           └→ 654 (v2.0.0 RC)
635 ────────────────────────────────┘
```

#648 was formally `blocked_by` #846. That edge was **stale** — #846's body was corrected earlier
today and states verbatim: *"This no longer blocks #648 … the desktop leg above is part of #648's
own wiring rather than a prerequisite to it."* Its three other declared deps (#884, #867, and the
original #647/#632/#630) are all closed. The native edge was dropped after verifying each.

Every other item in the deploy chain sits behind #648. Nothing else in the tracker unblocks eight
issues at once. **It leads this wave.**

The two long poles into #653 remain #635 (22 open children, 13 startable) and #642 (8 open, 4
startable). Neither closes in wave 6; the aim is to keep both draining while the deploy chain
starts moving.

## The batch — 8 PRs

Ownership is the batching unit, as always. The binding constraint this wave is
**`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs`**: six startable issues want it (#1107, #1108, #1025, #1076,
#1077, #1056). Exactly one may own it.

| PR | Track | Issues | Owns | Why here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | desktop | **648** | `apps/desktop/src-tauri/`, `crates/fuse/`, `crates/desktop-seams/` | **Critical path.** Unblocks #649/#650/#651/#652/#653/#654/#656. See the size caveat below |
| **2** | rotation | **1108** | `rotation/rotate_write.rs`, `net/rotation.rs` | Sole `net/rotation.rs` owner this wave. Unblocks **#1019 and #764**, more than any rival claimant |
| **3** | eng-foundation | **1102** | `gate/adoption.rs`, `net/author.rs` | **Live crypto DoS**, ~1000× amplification, ~1.32M Ed25519 verifications per record. Deliberately scoped out of #1050; nothing else covers it |
| **4** | write-plane | **1106** | `facade.rs`, `sync/rebase.rs`, `sync/drain.rs` | **Silent data loss** — a content write clobbers a concurrent version. Sole owner of both hot sync files. Unblocks #1094 → #1095 |
| **5** | write-plane | **849 + 850 + 851** | `content/retention.rs`, `content/dag.rs`, `content/profile.rs`, `apps/api/src/registry/` | Three issues, one file. **Closes umbrella #872 outright** |
| **6** | rotation | **1015** | `grants/invite.rs`, `grants/ledger.rs`, `mailbox/mod.rs` | File-disjoint from PR-2 — no `net/rotation.rs`, no `grants/create.rs`. Unblocks **#1016 and #1020** |
| **7** | web | **1091 + 1087** | `SelectionActionBar.tsx`, `hooks/useVaultActions.ts`, `routes/FilesPage.tsx` | Both under #642, the other long pole into #653. Disjoint files |
| **8** | web/client | **1063 + 1097** | `client/src/sw/pipe.ts`, `media/service.ts`, `media/broker.ts` | **Must ship together** — both rewrite `sw/pipe.ts`. Splitting them recreates the wave-4 duplicate-merge hazard |

content.text:
## Area 0 — Structural facts (context for all four)

- `crates/fuse` has exactly 7 source files, all read above; total 1,426 lines. It depends on **only** `cipherbox-engine` (`crates/fuse/Cargo.toml:11`).
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/` contains **one file**: `main.rs` (107 lines). Its manifest depends on `tauri` alone — **no** `cipherbox-engine`, `cipherbox-fuse`, or `cipherbox-desktop-seams` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:19-20`). Its own doc comment says so: "Scaffold only: no engine wiring, no login, no mount, no vault semantics" (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:4`).
- **No host adapter implementation exists anywhere.** `HostAdapter` is a trait only (`crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs:77-83`); the only implementor in-repo is the test `RecordingAdapter` (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:45-56`). No FUSE-T, no libfuse3, no WinFsp wire code.
- `crates/desktop-seams` has 10 modules; `staging_store.rs`, `snapshot_cache.rs`, `fs_util.rs`, `paths.rs` are all complete and fsync-barriered.

---

## Blueprint — the normative sentences (quote these verbatim in the sub-issues)

**Never-block law** — `blueprint/desktop.md:154-157`:
> "a kernel callback may block on **local durability** (op-queue fsync) and on **content-chunk fetches for uncached reads** — never on IPNS resolution, publish, rotation, or any API bookkeeping call."

**Read** — `blueprint/desktop.md:167-172`:
> "the engine maps the range onto sealed chunks, serves cached chunks immediately, fetches missing ones … First byte no longer waits for the last byte. A bounded in-memory plaintext chunk cache (LRU, zeroized on unmount) lives in the FS core for hot-file performance — the one place plaintext is cached, memory-only."

**Write** — `blueprint/desktop.md:173-177`:
> "bytes land in a per-handle **sealed spill file**: XChaCha20 under a random per-handle key held only in engine/FS memory, in the engine data dir."

**Release / journal ack** — `blueprint/desktop.md:178-184`:
> "**release** (and create/mkdir/rename/unlink/rmdir) — becomes exactly one facade intent op … A kernel rename is one `move`, which carries the relink, the rename, and the destination it replaces, so a replace is never observable half-done. The kernel is acked when the op is **journaled durably in the StagingStore** — the v1 INV-1 no-false-ack discipline."

**Over-budget errnos** — `blueprint/desktop.md:187-191`:
> "the offline staging budget running out (#33 D6 fail-fast) is `ENOSPC` and a hosted-quota refusal is `EDQUOT`."

**Dead letters** — `blueprint/desktop.md:201-205`:
> "**Dead-letters** … surface as a tray notification + a persistent tray section with the staged bytes recoverable to a local 'recovered files' export; nothing is silently dropped and the kernel is never retro-failed (it was acked at journal time — the dead-letter surface is the compensation channel)."

**Scope-exit refusal** — `blueprint/desktop.md:206-212`:
> "The refusal path (rotation impossible, fail-closed) rejects the **op at journal time** — the one mutation class where the ack waits on more than the fsync: the engine must accept the op before the kernel hears success. EIO with a tray explanation."

**Freshness** — `blueprint/desktop.md:219-232`:
> "Every lookup/readdir/getattr checks the target's snapshot age against the sync timing profile's staleness threshold; a stale hit fires a refresh hint for that node — this is the **FUSE-op TTL check** … The **focus window** is derived from the op stream: folders with FUSE traffic inside the profile's focus horizon count as 'open' … When a background reconcile lands a new snapshot, the engine event stream drives the **push-invalidation callback**."

---

## Area 1 — READ PATH

### EXISTS
- Nothing in the FUSE layer. There is **no `read` operation at all** in `OperationCore` — grep for `fn read` in `crates/fuse/src` returns only `readdir` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:98`).
- Handle bookkeeping only: `open` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:192-200`) validates the node is a file and mints a `HandleId`; `HandleTable::open` stores `{node, access}` and nothing else (`crates/fuse/src/handle.rs:55-60`). The handle is explicitly key-free by design (`crates/fuse/src/handle.rs:1-3`).
- The **engine** already provides the ranged primitives the read path would consume:
  - `Engine::open_content_stream` — pins head version + verified root manifest per handle (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2930`).
  - `Engine::read_stream(handle, offset, length)` — "fetching only the leaves the window covers" (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2962`).
  - `Engine::close_stream` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2993`), `MAX_OPEN_STREAMS` ceiling → `EngineError::TooManyStreams` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2938`).
  - `Engine::read_content` whole-file read (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2895`) and `leaf_range_for_byte_range` (`crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:297`).
- Error mapping for read failures is pre-wired: `ContentUnavailable → VfsError::Unavailable`, `TooManyStreams → Unavailable`, `UnsupportedContentFormat → Unavailable` (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:69-83`).

### MISSING
- No `OperationCore::read` / ranged chunk read — `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` has no such fn (file ends at line 389).
- No plaintext LRU chunk cache anywhere. Grep for `lru|Lru|LRU` across `crates/fuse` returns zero hits.
- No bounding and no zeroize-on-unmount. Grep for `zeroize|Zeroiz` across `crates/fuse` returns zero hits; `crates/fuse/Cargo.toml` has no `zeroize` dependency.
- No sealed spill files, no ephemeral XChaCha20 per-handle key. Grep `spill|XChaCha` in `crates/fuse` → zero hits. `OpenFile` carries only `{node, access}` (`crates/fuse/src/handle.rs:33-38`).
- "First byte before last byte" streaming is not wired at all — no `StreamHandle` is ever stored in `HandleTable` (`crates/fuse/src/handle.rs:42-45`), so there is no per-handle stream lifetime for `open_content_stream` to attach to.
- `size: Option<u64>` is projected through (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:34`, `:263`) but no read consumes it.

---

## Area 2 — WRITE PATH + JOURNAL ACK

### EXISTS — per operation
| Op | Where | Facade ops emitted |
|---|---|---|
| `create` | `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:117-126` → `make` `:268-296` | **exactly one** `Command::Create` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:280`) |
| `mkdir` | `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:129-131` → same `make` | **exactly one** `Command::Create` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:280`) |
| `unlink` | `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:134-136` → `remove` `:298-311` → `delete` `:319-322` | one `Command::Delete` for a plain file (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:321`) |
| `rmdir` | `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:139-141` → same path | **one op only in the common case**; a junk-holding folder emits N extra `Command::Delete` ops via `delete_descendants` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:326-338`, loop at `:334`). Deliberate and documented at `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:313-318` |
| `rename` | `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:145-189` | **one** `Command::Move` carrying `{node, new_parent, new_name, replacing}` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:176-182`) |
| `release` | `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:208-211` | **zero ops** — it only calls `HandleTable::close` |

- **#884 verified CLOSED and landed.** `Command::Move { node, new_parent, new_name, replacing }` exists in the facade (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:427-441`, doc: "Relink and rename a node in one intent op, conditionally replacing the node at the destination name"), is handled at `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2231-2258` and produces a single `Op::move_node` with a `Replaced { node, sequence }` conditional-delete anchor (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2249-2253`). The FUSE `rename` issues exactly that one op (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:176`). Caveat: when the destination is a *junk-holding* folder being replaced, `delete_descendants` fires extra `Delete` ops **before** the `Move` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:169`) — the move itself stays one op; only hidden junk costs more.
- **No false-ack.** `OperationCore::command` awaits `Engine::command` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:232-235`) → `stage_and_notify` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:3194-3204`) → `stage_op` (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs:50-65`) → `StagingStore::enqueue_op` (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs:64`) → desktop impl `FileStagingStore::enqueue_op` which does a durable counter write then `atomic_write` of the op record (`crates/desktop-seams/src/staging_store.rs:100-117`), and `atomic_write` is fsync-barriered (`crates/desktop-seams/src/fs_util.rs:1-7` doc; `crates/desktop-seams/src/staging_store.rs:36-43` doc). Every mutation returns only after that. **No acking-before-durability path found.**
- Rename atomicity under queue failure is already tested (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:361-389`), as is the no-op self-rename spending no journal entry (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:391-403`).

### MISSING
- **`release` produces no `updateContent` op** — the blueprint's core write requirement. `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:208-211` closes the handle and returns `Ok(())`. Nothing calls `Engine::begin_write` / `push_chunk` / `commit_write` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2344`, `:2461`, `:2521`) from anywhere in `crates/fuse`.
- No `OperationCore::write` at all (grep `fn write` in `crates/fuse/src` → only a test name at `crates/fuse/src/handle.rs:124`).
- No `flush`, `fsync`, `setattr`, or `truncate` operations in `ops.rs`.
- `Access::writable()` exists (`crates/fuse/src/handle.rs:26-28`) but is **never called** in `crates/fuse/src` — write-permission enforcement on a handle is unwired.
- `WriteHandle` / `WriteTarget` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:95`, `:110`) are never referenced by the fuse crate.
- `InodeTable::forget` exists (`crates/fuse/src/inode.rs:66-73`) but `OperationCore` exposes no `forget` op to adapters.

---

## Area 3 — REFUSAL PATHS

### EXISTS
- **Vocabulary and mapping, no plumbing.** `VfsError::OverBudget(OverBudgetCause)` (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:36`) re-exports the engine cause (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:10`), and `EngineError::OverBudget { cause, .. } → VfsError::OverBudget(cause)` (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:68`). The errno decision is explicitly deferred to the adapter: "`ENOSPC` for a full device, `EDQUOT` for a full account" (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:7-9`).
- Cause preservation across the boundary is tested for all six causes (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:190-209`).
- **Engine-side staging budget refusal exists**: `begin_write` reads `staged_bytes_total()` and calls `writes.ledger.admit(requested, staged, &self.storage_policy)` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2367-2378`); `Refused → EngineError::OverBudget` maps `OverLimit→StagingLimit`, `DeviceFull→DeviceFull`, `Backlog→StagingBacklog`, `TooManyWrites→TooManyWrites`, `Unmeasured→StorageUnmeasured` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1294-1313`; refusal logic `crates/engine/src/content/budget.rs:109-115`).
- **Hosted-quota preflight exists**: `self.hosted_quota_pre_flight(requested)` is called in `begin_write` before admission (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2366`), and yields `OverBudgetCause::AccountQuota` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2448-2456`).
- **What #867 left in the engine** (all present, all consumable):
  - `Event::DeadLetter { op_id, reason }` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:571-577`) with 8 `DeadLetterReason` variants (`crates/engine/src/sync/…`, re-exported `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:96`).
  - `SnapshotView.dead_letters: Vec<DeadLetter>` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:265`), `DeadLetter { op_id, reason }` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:236-241`).
  - `SnapshotView.blocked: Option<BlockedOp>` — over-quota drain hold, deliberately state-not-event (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:266-270`); `BlockedOp { op_id, node, needed_bytes }` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:318-325`).
  - `SnapshotView.retained_records: usize` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:271-277`), `SnapshotView.staleness` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:279`).
  - Dead-letter staged-byte preservation keyed for recovery (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs:67-75`).
  - Proof it is a live, consumable surface: the **wasm/web** binding already consumes all of it (`crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:177-209`, `:337-339`, `:358-372`, `:456-461`, `:681`).

### MISSING
- **The FUSE layer consumes none of #867's output.** Grep for `dead_letter|DeadLetter|BlockedOp|snapshot(` across `crates/fuse/src` → zero hits. `OperationCore` only ever calls `engine.view()` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:223`), which returns `EngineView` — a view that carries **no** `dead_letters`, `blocked`, `retained_records`, or `staleness` fields (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:966-1006`). `Engine::snapshot()` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2809`), the only accessor that carries them, is never called from the fuse crate.
- No ENOSPC/EDQUOT emission path: no adapter exists to do the errno mapping, and nothing in `crates/fuse` ever reaches `begin_write`, so `OverBudgetCause` can never actually be produced through the mount today.
- **No scope-exit refusal at journal time.** `stage_and_notify` performs no scope-exit check — it seals, enqueues, emits `SnapshotUpdated`, returns (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:3194-3204`). Scope-exit is detected at **rebase/drain** time instead (`crates/engine/src/sync/rebase.rs:53-55`, `:139`, `:247-259`, `:303-304`). So the blueprint's "the one mutation class where the ack waits on more than the fsync" (`blueprint/desktop.md:209-212`) is **not implemented** at either layer, and there is no EIO refusal.
- `VfsError` has no variant that an adapter would naturally map to EIO for a journal-time refusal; the closest is `Internal` (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:48-53`), which is a host-local-failure classification, not a fail-closed rotation refusal.
- No dead-letter surfacing hooks to a tray: `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` has no event-stream subscription (the whole file is tray/window chrome, `:19-107`).

---

## Area 4 — FRESHNESS

### EXISTS
- **Kernel-reply TTL derivation only.** `CacheTtls::for_host` picks `profile.stale_after` when the adapter can push, else `profile.poll_cadence` (`crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs:58-68`); surfaced as `OperationCore::cache_ttls()` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:71-73`). Never-zero is enforced by test (`crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs:121-130`).
- **Push invalidation is wired for locally-originated mutations.** `Invalidation::{Data, Attributes, Entry}` (`crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs:15-33`); `entry_changed` fires on create/mkdir (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:294`), unlink/rmdir (`:309`), rename both sides plus attrs (`:185-187`); root re-anchor fires `Attributes { ino: ROOT_INO }` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:224-227`, driven by `InodeTable::bind_root` returning "moved" at `crates/fuse/src/inode.rs:45-60`).
- **Engine-side freshness machinery all exists**: `Command::SetFocus { node }` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:449-453`) handled at `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2261-2270`, calling `refresh_focus_on_access` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2301-2331`) which uses `focus_folders_due(...)` against the profile; `FocusWindow` (`crates/engine/src/sync/tick.rs:34`), `FocusTarget` (`:44`), `focus_set` (`:87`); `Command::ManualRefresh` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:455`); `EventStream::{next, try_next}` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:945-957`); `Event::SnapshotUpdated` / `StalenessChanged` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:559-566`); the `RefreshHintSource` seam trait (`crates/engine/src/seams/refresh_hint.rs:21-25`).

### MISSING
- **No FUSE-op TTL check.** `lookup` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:76-84`), `getattr` (`:87-92`), and `readdir` (`:98-114`) each just call `render()` and return; none reads a snapshot age, none compares against `stale_after`, none fires a refresh hint. `cache_ttls()` is a kernel-reply value, **not** the blueprint's per-op staleness check.
- **No focus window derived from the op stream.** `Command::SetFocus` is never issued from `crates/fuse` (grep `SetFocus|focus` in `crates/fuse/src` → zero hits outside the word "stale" in comments). Nothing tracks which folders saw recent FUSE traffic.
- **No engine-event-stream-driven push invalidation.** `EventStream` is never referenced in `crates/fuse` (grep → zero hits). Every `adapter.invalidate(...)` call in `ops.rs` is triggered synchronously by a *local* mutation; a background reconcile landing a new snapshot invalidates nothing. This is the exact gap the blueprint names at `blueprint/desktop.md:228-232`.
- **`RefreshHintSource` has no desktop implementation.** `crates/desktop-seams/src/lib.rs:23-27` says so explicitly: "refresh hints are produced by the `crates/fuse` operation core from FUSE-op TTL checks" — and those checks do not exist. `crates/desktop-seams/src/lib.rs:36-44` lists the nine modules; there is no `refresh_hint.rs`.
- `Invalidation::Data { ino }` (`crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs:17-20`) is declared but **never constructed** anywhere in `crates/fuse/src` — consistent with there being no content path.
- No `noattrcache` mount-option handling anywhere (grep → zero hits in `crates`/`apps`), which `blueprint/desktop.md:236-239` makes a hard requirement.

---

## Test coverage — the `fuse-op-core` suite

- **Location**: `crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs`, 713 lines, **29 `#[test]` functions** (all sync, driven via a `poll_once`/`block_on` helper at `crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:126`). Self-identified at `crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:1`: "The `fuse-op-core` suite: every vfs operation driven against a real engine".
- **Harness**: real `Engine<FakeSeamTypes>` over in-memory seam fakes + virtual clock (`crates/fuse/Cargo.toml:13-15`); `RecordingAdapter` implements `HostAdapter` and records invalidations (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:32-56`); `InMemoryStagingStore::fail_enqueue_after(n)` injects durable-queue outages (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:75`).
- **CI gate name**: there is **no job named `fuse-op-core`**. **Never-block law** — `blueprint/desktop.md:154-157`:
> "a kernel callback may block on **local durability** (op-queue fsync) and on **content-chunk fetches for uncached reads** — never on IPNS resolution, publish, rotation, or any API bookkeeping call."

**Read** — `blueprint/desktop.md:167-172`:
> "the engine maps the range onto sealed chunks, serves cached chunks immediately, fetches missing ones … First byte no longer waits for the last byte. A bounded in-memory plaintext chunk cache (LRU, zeroized on unmount) lives in the FS core for hot-file performance — the one place plaintext is cached, memory-only."

**Write** — `blueprint/desktop.md:173-177`:
> "bytes land in a per-handle **sealed spill file**: XChaCha20 under a random per-handle key held only in engine/FS memory, in the engine data dir."

**Release / journal ack** — `blueprint/desktop.md:178-184`:
> "**release** (and create/mkdir/rename/unlink/rmdir) — becomes exactly one facade intent op … A kernel rename is one `move`, which carries the relink, the rename, and the destination it replaces, so a replace is never observable half-done. The kernel is acked when the op is **journaled durably in the StagingStore** — the v1 INV-1 no-false-ack discipline."

**Over-budget errnos** — `blueprint/desktop.md:187-191`:
> "the offline staging budget running out (#33 D6 fail-fast) is `ENOSPC` and a hosted-quota refusal is `EDQUOT`."

**Dead letters** — `blueprint/desktop.md:201-205`:
> "**Dead-letters** … surface as a tray notification + a persistent tray section with the staged bytes recoverable to a local 'recovered files' export; nothing is silently dropped and the kernel is never retro-failed (it was acked at journal time — the dead-letter surface is the compensation channel)."

**Scope-exit refusal** — `blueprint/desktop.md:206-212`:
> "The refusal path (rotation impossible, fail-closed) rejects the **op at journal time** — the one mutation class where the ack waits on more than the fsync: the engine must accept the op before the kernel hears success. EIO with a tray explanation."

**Freshness** — `blueprint/desktop.md:219-232`:
> "Every lookup/readdir/getattr checks the target's snapshot age against the sync timing profile's staleness threshold; a stale hit fires a refresh hint for that node — this is the **FUSE-op TTL check** … The **focus window** is derived from the op stream: folders with FUSE traffic inside the profile's focus horizon count as 'open' … When a background reconcile lands a new snapshot, the engine event stream drives the **push-invalidation callback**."

## Already landed — do not re-implement

The **engine** side of ranged reads is complete and tested. Do not build a parallel path:

- `Engine::open_content_stream` pins the head version and a verified root manifest per handle (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2930`), with a `MAX_OPEN_STREAMS` ceiling surfacing as `EngineError::TooManyStreams` (`:2938`).
- `Engine::read_stream(handle, offset, length)` fetches only the leaves the window covers (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2962`); `Engine::close_stream` releases it (`:2993`).
- `leaf_range_for_byte_range` maps a byte window onto sealed chunks (`crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:297`).
- Error mapping is already wired: `ContentUnavailable`, `TooManyStreams` and `UnsupportedContentFormat` all map to `VfsError::Unavailable` (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:69-83`).

The `fuse-op-core` suite already proves the **metadata** surface never yields (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:211-242`), and `open` mints a handle after a kind check (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:192-200`).

## Scope

`crates/fuse` has **no read operation at all** — grep for `fn read` in `crates/fuse/src` returns only `readdir` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:98`). Land it.

1. **`OperationCore::read(handle, offset, size)`** over the engine stream primitives above. The blueprint is normative (`blueprint/desktop.md:167-172`): *"the engine maps the range onto sealed chunks, serves cached chunks immediately, fetches missing ones … First byte no longer waits for the last byte."*

2. **Per-handle stream lifetime.** `HandleTable` stores only `{node, access}` today (`crates/fuse/src/handle.rs:33-38`, `:55-60`), so there is nowhere for `open_content_stream`'s handle to live. Attach it, and release it in `release` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:208-211`). The handle is deliberately key-free (`crates/fuse/src/handle.rs:1-3`) — keep it that way; a stream id is not key material.

3. **The bounded plaintext LRU chunk cache**, zeroized on unmount. `blueprint/desktop.md:170-172`: *"A bounded in-memory plaintext chunk cache (LRU, zeroized on unmount) lives in the FS core for hot-file performance — the one place plaintext is cached, memory-only."* There is no LRU and no zeroize anywhere in `crates/fuse` today (no `lru`/`zeroize` hits; `crates/fuse/Cargo.toml` has neither dependency). Zeroize at the terminal owner only — the cache owns these buffers, so it zeroes them; it must not zero a buffer the engine still owns (AGENTS.md rule 7).

4. **Wire `Invalidation::Data { ino }`** (`crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs:17-20`), which is declared but never constructed — consistent with there being no content path today.

### An open design question this issue must settle

The blueprint says the cache lives *"in the FS core"*, but the engine already owns `StreamHandle` pinning and leaf fetching (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2930-2992`). Nothing in the repo resolves whether the cache sits above or below the facade. **Decide explicitly and record the reasoning in the PR** — a plaintext cache below the facade would put plaintext in the engine, which the blueprint's "the one place plaintext is cached" sentence appears to forbid.

### Not in scope

Writes, spill files, refusal errnos and freshness — the sibling issues below. No host adapter (that is #648's own stated boundary).

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/desktop.md`: Reads (`:167-172`); the never-block law (`:154-157`) — *"a kernel callback may block on local durability (op-queue fsync) and on content-chunk fetches for uncached reads — never on IPNS resolution, publish, rotation, or any API bookkeeping call."*

`CONTEXT.md`: focus window, sealed chunk, staging store.

## Gate

Extend `crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs` (29 tests today, none covering reads):

- a ranged read returns the correct bytes for a window spanning a chunk boundary
- first byte before last byte: a read of the first chunk completes without fetching the last
- an uncached read may block on the chunk fetch; **no read path ever blocks on resolve, publish or rotation** — the never-block law, asserted the way `the_read_surface_never_yields` already asserts it for metadata (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:211`)
- the LRU is bounded: reading more distinct chunks than the bound evicts, and total retained plaintext stays under it
- unmount zeroizes the cache
- `release` closes the engine stream — opening and releasing more than `MAX_OPEN_STREAMS` times in sequence never exhausts the ceiling
- a read on a handle whose content is unavailable surfaces `VfsError::Unavailable`, not a hang

**The `fuse-op-core` suite has no named CI gate.** It runs inside the workspace sweep on `cargo-linux`/`cargo-macos`/`cargo-windows` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:421`, `:656`, `:683`). AGENTS.md testing law 1 requires a named gate the day a suite lands. Add one as part of this issue, since it is the first of the four to touch the suite.

## Depends on

Nothing outstanding.

## Blocks

The three sibling slices — all four own `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` and `handle.rs`, so they are strictly sequential, never parallel.

Part of #648

## Already landed — do not re-implement

**The metadata write path is done, and the no-false-ack law already holds.** Verified against `main` @ `a798ebf4e`:

| Op | Site | Facade ops |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create` / `mkdir` | `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:117-131` → `make` `:268-296` | exactly one `Command::Create` (`:280`) |
| `unlink` / `rmdir` | `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:134-141` → `remove` `:298-311` | one `Command::Delete` (`:321`) |
| `rename` | `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:145-189` | **one** `Command::Move { node, new_parent, new_name, replacing }` (`:176-182`) |

**#884 landed and is verified**: `Command::Move` exists (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:427-441`), is handled at `:2231-2258`, and produces a single `Op::move_node` with a `Replaced { node, sequence }` conditional-delete anchor (`:2249-2253`). A kernel rename really is one atomic op.

**No false-ack exists anywhere.** `OperationCore::command` awaits `Engine::command` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:232-235`) → `stage_and_notify` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:3194`) → `stage_op` (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs:50-65`) → `FileStagingStore::enqueue_op`, which does a durable counter write then an fsync-barriered `atomic_write` (`crates/desktop-seams/src/staging_store.rs:100-117`). Rename atomicity under a failing durable queue is already tested (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:361-389`), as is a self-rename spending no journal entry (`:391-403`).

**Do not re-litigate any of that.** This issue is the *content* write path only.

## Scope

`release` closes the handle and returns `Ok(())` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:208-211`). It emits **zero** ops. There is no `write`, `flush`, `fsync`, `setattr` or `truncate` in `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` at all, and nothing in the crate ever calls `Engine::begin_write` / `push_chunk` / `commit_write` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2344`, `:2461`, `:2521`).

1. **`OperationCore::write(handle, offset, data)`** landing bytes in a **per-handle sealed spill file**. `blueprint/desktop.md:173-177` is normative: *"bytes land in a per-handle sealed spill file: XChaCha20 under a random per-handle key held only in engine/FS memory, in the engine data dir."* The key is ephemeral and memory-only — it is never persisted, never logged, and is zeroized when the handle closes (AGENTS.md rules 1, 2, 7). Entropy enters through the injected seam, never a direct RNG call (AGENTS.md rule 3).

2. **`release` becomes exactly one `updateContent` intent op**, acked at journal time. `blueprint/desktop.md:178-184`: *"The kernel is acked when the op is journaled durably in the StagingStore — the v1 INV-1 no-false-ack discipline."* Drive it through `begin_write` / `push_chunk` / `commit_write` against `WriteHandle`/`WriteTarget` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:95`, `:110`), which the fuse crate does not reference today.

3. **`flush`, `fsync`, `setattr`, `truncate`.** A `truncate` to zero on an open handle must not be silently lost — decide and state whether it is a spill-file operation or its own intent op.

4. **Enforce write permission.** `Access::writable()` exists (`crates/fuse/src/handle.rs:26-28`) but is **never called** in `crates/fuse/src`. A write on a read-only handle must be refused, not accepted and dropped.

### Note on `rmdir` and the "exactly one op" reading

The plain cases emit one op, but a junk-holding folder emits N extra `Command::Delete` ops through `delete_descendants` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:326-338`), documented as deliberate at `:313-318`. That is pre-existing and **not** in scope here; flagging it so a reviewer does not read it as a regression this slice introduced.

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/desktop.md`: Writes (`:173-177`); release and journal ack (`:178-184`); the never-block law (`:154-157`).

`CONTEXT.md`: staging store, intent op, op queue, write handle.

## Gate

Extend `fuse-op-core`. It has **zero** coverage of `release`, write or `updateContent` today, because none exist:

- a write-then-release produces **exactly one** `updateContent` op, and the bytes round-trip through a read
- the kernel is acked only after the op is durably journaled — inject a `fail_enqueue_after(n)` outage (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:75`) and assert the write is refused rather than acked
- the spill file is sealed at rest: assert the plaintext does not appear in the spill file's bytes
- the per-handle key is zeroized on release, and two handles to the same node get **different** keys
- a write on a read-only handle is refused
- a crash between spill and release loses the unreleased write and leaves no partial op in the queue
- release with no writes emits no op

## Depends on

The read-path slice — both own `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` and `handle.rs`, and the stream lifetime it adds to `HandleTable` is where the spill-file state also belongs.

## Blocks

The refusal-paths slice: `ENOSPC`/`EDQUOT` can only be produced through the mount once something in `crates/fuse` actually reaches `begin_write`.

**#867 left a complete, consumable surface in the engine.** All of it exists; none of it is wired to the mount:

- `Event::DeadLetter { op_id, reason }` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:571-577`) with 8 `DeadLetterReason` variants.
- `SnapshotView.dead_letters: Vec<DeadLetter>` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:265`), `DeadLetter { op_id, reason }` (`:236-241`).
- `SnapshotView.blocked: Option<BlockedOp>` — the over-quota drain hold, deliberately state-not-event (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:266-270`); `BlockedOp { op_id, node, needed_bytes }` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:318-325`).
- Dead-letter staged bytes are preserved keyed for recovery (`crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs:67-75`).
- **Proof it is consumable**: the wasm/web binding already consumes all of it (`crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:177-209`, `:337-339`, `:358-372`, `:456-461`).

**The budget refusal machinery also exists.** `begin_write` calls `hosted_quota_pre_flight` then `writes.ledger.admit(...)` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:2366-2378`); `Refused` maps to `EngineError::OverBudget` with `OverLimit→StagingLimit`, `DeviceFull→DeviceFull`, `Backlog→StagingBacklog`, `TooManyWrites→TooManyWrites`, `Unmeasured→StorageUnmeasured` (`:1294-1313`), and hosted quota yields `OverBudgetCause::AccountQuota` (`:2448-2456`). `VfsError::OverBudget(OverBudgetCause)` re-exports the cause and its preservation across the boundary is tested for all six causes (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:36`, `:68`, `:190-209`).

Do not rebuild any of this.

## Scope

Three gaps, one of which needs an **engine-side** change.

1. **The FUSE layer consumes none of #867's output.** `OperationCore` only ever calls `engine.view()` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:223`), and `EngineView` carries no `dead_letters`, `blocked`, `retained_records` or `staleness` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:966-1006`). `Engine::snapshot()` (`:2809`) — the accessor that does — is never called from `crates/fuse`. Wire the surfacing hooks. `blueprint/desktop.md:201-205`: *"nothing is silently dropped and the kernel is never retro-failed (it was acked at journal time — the dead-letter surface is the compensation channel)."*

2. **Errno mapping at the boundary.** `blueprint/desktop.md:187-191`: *"the offline staging budget running out (#33 D6 fail-fast) is `ENOSPC` and a hosted-quota refusal is `EDQUOT`."* `crates/fuse/src/error.rs:7-9` deliberately defers the errno decision to the adapter — keep that seam, but make the classification unambiguous so an adapter cannot get it wrong, and cover it.

3. **The scope-exit refusal at journal time is not implemented at either layer.** This is the real work. `stage_and_notify` seals, enqueues, emits `SnapshotUpdated` and returns, with no scope-exit check (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:3194-3204`); scope exit is detected at **rebase/drain** time instead (`crates/engine/src/sync/rebase.rs:53-55`, `:139`, `:247-259`). The blueprint requires the opposite (`blueprint/desktop.md:206-212`):

   > *"The refusal path (rotation impossible, fail-closed) rejects the **op at journal time** — the one mutation class where the ack waits on more than the fsync: the engine must accept the op before the kernel hears success. EIO with a tray explanation."*

   This is a **fail-closed trust boundary** (AGENTS.md rule 6), so it fails closed by construction: if the engine cannot determine that the op is safe to accept, it refuses. `VfsError` has no variant an adapter would map to EIO for this — `Internal` (`crates/fuse/src/error.rs:48-53`) classifies a host-local failure, not a fail-closed refusal. **Add the variant**; do not overload `Internal`.

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/desktop.md`: Conflicts, dead letters, and rotation (`:201-212`); over-budget errnos (`:187-191`); release and journal ack (`:178-184`).

`CONTEXT.md`: dead letter, staging budget, scope exit, adoption gate.

## Gate

Extend `fuse-op-core`. It has **no** ENOSPC/EDQUOT/EIO/dead-letter coverage today — the only refusal coverage is the mapping unit tests at `crates/fuse/src/error.rs:140-235`:

- staging-budget exhaustion surfaces `OverBudgetCause::StagingLimit`/`DeviceFull` and classifies as ENOSPC; a hosted-quota refusal classifies as EDQUOT. Distinct, asserted outcomes — not one bucket.
- a dead-lettered op reaches the surfacing hook with its `DeadLetterReason` intact, and its staged bytes stay recoverable
- a blocked op surfaces as state, not as a kernel failure — the kernel is **never retro-failed** for an op already acked at journal time
- **a scope-exiting mutation is refused at journal time**: the op is not enqueued, the kernel sees the EIO-class refusal, and the queue is unchanged afterwards
- the refusal is fail-closed — an engine that cannot classify the op refuses it rather than accepting it
- an over-budget refusal spends no journal entry and holds no partial state

## Depends on

The write-path slice — nothing in `crates/fuse` reaches `begin_write` today, so `OverBudgetCause` cannot be produced through the mount until it does.

Note this slice edits `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`, a hot file. Do not run it concurrently with another `facade.rs` owner.

## Blocks

Nothing tracked.

input.content:
## Already landed — do not re-implement

**Kernel-reply TTL derivation exists.** `CacheTtls::for_host` picks `profile.stale_after` when the adapter can push and `profile.poll_cadence` when it cannot (`crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs:58-68`), surfaced as `OperationCore::cache_ttls()` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:71-73`), with never-zero enforced by test (`crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs:121-130`). **This is a kernel-reply value, not the blueprint's per-op staleness check** — do not mistake one for the other.

**Push invalidation for locally-originated mutations exists.** `Invalidation::{Data, Attributes, Entry}` (`crates/fuse/src/adapter.rs:15-33`); `entry_changed` fires on create/mkdir (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:294`), unlink/rmdir (`:309`), rename on both sides plus attrs (`:185-187`), and a root re-anchor fires `Attributes { ino: ROOT_INO }` (`:224-227`). Covered by `every_mutation_pushes_an_invalidation_at_the_mount` (`crates/fuse/tests/fuse_op_core.rs:522-570`) and `a_refused_operation_pushes_nothing` (`:571-586`).

**The engine-side freshness machinery all exists**: `Command::SetFocus { node }` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:449-453`) handled at `:2261-2270` via `refresh_focus_on_access` (`:2301-2331`); `FocusWindow`/`FocusTarget`/`focus_set` (`crates/engine/src/sync/tick.rs:34`, `:44`, `:87`); `Command::ManualRefresh` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:455`); `EventStream::{next, try_next}` (`:945-957`); `Event::SnapshotUpdated` / `StalenessChanged` (`:559-566`); the `RefreshHintSource` seam trait (`crates/engine/src/seams/refresh_hint.rs:21-25`).

**None of it is connected to the mount.** That is this issue.

## Scope

1. **The FUSE-op TTL check.** `lookup` (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:76-84`), `getattr` (`:87-92`) and `readdir` (`:98-114`) each call `render()` and return. None reads a snapshot age, none compares against `stale_after`, none fires a refresh hint. `blueprint/desktop.md:219-232`: *"Every lookup/readdir/getattr checks the target's snapshot age against the sync timing profile's staleness threshold; a stale hit fires a refresh hint for that node — this is the FUSE-op TTL check."*

2. **The focus window derived from the op stream.** `Command::SetFocus` is never issued from `crates/fuse` — nothing tracks which folders saw recent FUSE traffic. Blueprint: *"folders with FUSE traffic inside the profile's focus horizon count as 'open'."*

3. **Event-stream-driven push invalidation.** `EventStream` is never referenced in `crates/fuse`. Every `adapter.invalidate(...)` call today is triggered synchronously by a *local* mutation, so a background reconcile landing a new snapshot invalidates nothing. Blueprint: *"When a background reconcile lands a new snapshot, the engine event stream drives the push-invalidation callback."*

4. **A desktop `RefreshHintSource`.** There is no implementation. `crates/desktop-seams/src/lib.rs:23-27` states the intended design — *"refresh hints are produced by the `crates/fuse` operation core from FUSE-op TTL checks"* — and those checks do not exist, so the seam has no producer.

5. **`noattrcache` mount-option handling**, which `blueprint/desktop.md:236-239` makes a hard requirement. Zero hits across `crates/` and `apps/` today.

### Determinism

The staleness comparison is a clock read. Time enters through the injected seam, never a direct clock call (AGENTS.md rule 3) — the `fuse-op-core` harness already runs on a virtual clock (`crates/fuse/Cargo.toml:13-15`), so a test that needs to age a snapshot advances that clock rather than sleeping.

## Blueprint anchors

`blueprint/desktop.md`: Freshness (`:219-232`); mount options (`:236-239`); the never-block law (`:154-157`) — a TTL check fires a **hint**, it never blocks the callback on a resolve.

`CONTEXT.md`: focus window, staleness threshold, pull-only focus-window polling, refresh hint.

## Gate

Extend `fuse-op-core`. It covers the adapter direction only today; there is **no** test of TTL checks, focus windows, or event-stream-driven invalidation, because none exist:

- a `lookup`/`getattr`/`readdir` against a snapshot older than `stale_after` fires a refresh hint for that node; one inside the threshold fires none
- **a stale hit never blocks** — the op returns from cache and the hint is asynchronous (the never-block law)
- FUSE traffic on a folder puts it in the focus set; traffic outside the focus horizon does not
- a background reconcile landing a new snapshot drives an invalidation at the mount **with no local mutation involved** — the gap `blueprint/desktop.md:228-232` names
- an adapter that cannot push gets the shorter cache TTL **and** still receives event-driven invalidations
- `noattrcache` suppresses attribute caching end-to-end

## Depends on

The refusal-paths slice — this slice adds TTL checks to `lookup`/`getattr`/`readdir` in `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs`, which all three earlier slices also edit. Strictly sequential.

## Blocks

Nothing tracked. This is the last of the four; **#648 closes when it lands.**

Part of #648

`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` and `handle.rs`, so they can never run in parallel — this is a pipeline,
not a fan-out, and only the first fits in wave 6.

|---|---|

| **#1110** | Content write path, per-handle sealed spill files, `release` as one `updateContent` op acked at journal time |
| **#1111** | Refusal paths: ENOSPC/EDQUOT, dead-letter + blocked surfacing, scope-exit refusal at journal time |
| **#1112** | Freshness: FUSE-op TTL checks, focus window from the op stream, event-stream push invalidation, `noattrcache` |

Chained `1109 → 1110 → 1111 → 1112`, all four parented to #648, all `comp:desktop`, milestone
v2.0.0, verified by read-back. **#648 closes when #1112 lands.**

Recon against `main` @ `a798ebf4e` reshaped the split from the naive read/write/freshness cut:

- **The metadata write path is already done.** create/mkdir/unlink/rmdir/rename each emit exactly
  one intent op (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:117-189`), and **no false-ack exists** — every mutation
  returns only after an fsync-barriered journal write (`crates/desktop-seams/src/staging_store.rs:100-117`).
  #884 is verified landed, so a kernel rename really is one `Command::Move`. What is missing is the
  **content** path: `release` emits zero ops today (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:208-211`).
- **#1111 needs an engine-side change**, not just FUSE. The scope-exit refusal at journal time is
  implemented at **neither** layer — `stage_and_notify` has no such check
  (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:3194-3204`) and scope exit is detected at rebase/drain time instead.
  It edits `facade.rs`, so it must not run concurrently with another `facade.rs` owner.
- **#867's output is consumable but unconsumed.** `SnapshotView.dead_letters`/`blocked` exist and
  the wasm binding already reads them; `crates/fuse` only calls `engine.view()`, which carries
  neither. Wiring, not invention.
- **The `fuse-op-core` suite has no named CI gate** — it rides the workspace sweep. AGENTS.md
  testing law 1 requires one. #1109 carries that obligation as the first slice to touch the suite.

There is also **no host adapter of any kind** — `HostAdapter` is a trait whose only implementor is a
test recorder, and `apps/desktop/src-tauri` does not depend on the engine at all. That stays out of
scope per #648's own "no adapters, no tray UI" boundary; it is #649's work.

#648 is split. Four sequential slices, all verified by read-back:

| Slice | Scope |
|---|---|
| **#1109** | Ranged read path, per-handle stream lifetime, bounded plaintext LRU zeroized on unmount |
| **#1110** | Content write path, sealed spill files, `release` as one `updateContent` op acked at journal time |
| **#1111** | Refusal paths: ENOSPC/EDQUOT, dead-letter + blocked surfacing, scope-exit refusal at journal time |
| **#1112** | Freshness: TTL checks, focus window, event-stream push invalidation, `noattrcache` |

Chained `1109 → 1110 → 1111 → 1112`, all parented to #648, `comp:desktop`, milestone v2.0.0. #648's body is rewritten as an umbrella and its stale #846 prose corrected. Its downstream edges to #649/#650 are intact.

**They're a pipeline, not a fan-out** — all four own `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` and `handle.rs`, so only #1109 fits in wave 6.

Recon reshaped the split away from the naive read/write/freshness cut:

- **The metadata write path is already done.** create/mkdir/unlink/rmdir/rename each emit exactly one intent op, and **no false-ack exists** — every mutation returns only after an fsync-barriered journal write. #884 landed, so a kernel rename really is one `Command::Move`. The gap is the *content* path: `release` emits zero ops today (`ops.rs:208-211`).
- **#1111 needs an engine-side change, not just FUSE.** The scope-exit refusal at journal time is implemented at *neither* layer — `stage_and_notify` has no such check, and scope exit is detected at rebase/drain time instead. So it touches `facade.rs` and can't run beside another `facade.rs` owner.
- **#867's output is consumable but unconsumed** — `SnapshotView.dead_letters`/`blocked` exist and the wasm binding already reads them; `crates/fuse` only calls `engine.view()`, which carries neither. Wiring, not invention.
- **`fuse-op-core` has no named CI gate** — 29 tests riding the workspace sweep, which AGENTS.md testing law 1 forbids. #1109 carries that obligation as the first slice to touch the suite.

One thing worth knowing about the wider picture: there's **no host adapter of any kind**. `HostAdapter` is a trait whose only implementor is a test recorder, and `apps/desktop/src-tauri` doesn't depend on the engine at all. That's correctly #649's work and outside #648's stated boundary — but it means nothing calls `OperationCore` through a real mount until #649 lands, so all four slices are gated by their test suite rather than by a running mount.

## Wave 6 — 8 PRs

Full plan at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-myankelev-Code-random-cipher-box/wave6-plan.md`.

| PR | Track | Issues | Owns | Why it's here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | desktop | **1109** | `crates/fuse/src/{ops,handle}.rs` | Critical path — first #648 slice, and everything downstream of #648 is schedule, not code |
| **2** | rotation | **1108** | `rotation/rotate_write.rs`, `net/rotation.rs` | Sole `net/rotation.rs` owner. Unblocks #1019 and #764 |
| **3** | eng-foundation | **1102** | `gate/adoption.rs`, `net/author.rs` | Live crypto DoS, ~1000× amplification |
| **4** | write-plane | **1106** | `facade.rs`, `sync/rebase.rs`, `sync/drain.rs` | Silent data loss. Sole owner of both hot sync files. Unblocks #1094 → #1095 |
| **5** | write-plane | **849 + 850 + 851** | `content/retention.rs`, `content/dag.rs` | Three issues, one file — closes umbrella #872 outright |
| **6** | rotation | **1015** | `grants/invite.rs`, `grants/ledger.rs`, `mailbox/mod.rs` | File-disjoint from PR-2. Unblocks #1016 and #1020 |
| **7** | web | **1091 + 1087** | `SelectionActionBar.tsx`, `useVaultActions.ts`, `FilesPage.tsx` | Both under #642, the other long pole into #653 |
| **8** | web/client | **1063 + 1097** | `client/src/sw/pipe.ts`, `media/service.ts` | Must ship together — both rewrite `sw/pipe.ts` |

**Merge order 1 → 8.** PR-2 lands early because `net/rotation.rs` is the file wave 5 fought over twice. PRs 3–8 are file-disjoint from each other and from 1–2.

## What shapes it

**The deploy path opened.** #648's `blocked_by` #846 was stale — #846's own body says so, and its three other deps are closed. Dropping that edge unblocked #649 → #650 → #651 → #653 staging cutover, plus #652/#654/#656. Nothing else in the tracker moves eight issues at once.

**`net/rotation.rs` is the binding constraint.** Six startable issues want it — #1107, #1108, #1025, #1076, #1077, #1056. #1108 takes it because it unblocks two downstream issues where #1107 unblocks one. The other four wait for wave 7, where #1107 and #1025 should pair.

**#648's four slices are a pipeline, not a fan-out.** All own `ops.rs` and `handle.rs`, so only #1109 fits this wave. #648 needs four waves to close, which is worth knowing when you look at the deploy chain — the cutover is further out than "unblocked" suggests.

## Held out, with reasons

- #1107, #1025, #1076, #1077, #1056 — all want `net/rotation.rs`
- #767 — a refactor of the exact files #635 is still rewriting; correct only once rotation settles
- #1073, #1085, #1060 — contend on `facade.rs` with PR-4
- #1059, #1090 — contend on `sync/drain.rs` with PR-4
- #914 — L, would likely subsume #1087; #1087 ships now since the bug is live and #914 isn't scheduled
- #831 — no contention, but the wave is already 8 PRs

**#1083 is the one I'd reconsider.** It became startable when #1052 closed, it's `client/src/leaderRelay.ts` (disjoint from PR-8), and it's a security item — an unauthenticated rendezvous on a shared origin channel. I left it out on batch size alone. Say the word and it's PR-9.

## Before launching

Three things carried from wave 5, none of them blockers but all of them cheap to get wrong:

- **`vars.STAGING_API_URL` doesn't exist at any scope** — needed before #653
- **macroscope credits are exhausted** — six of wave 5's seven PRs carried one bot verdict, not two. Worth topping up before a wave with a crypto tightening and a data-loss fix
- **`Web E2E Smoke Result` is a flaky required check** (`smoke.spec.ts:43`) — re-run before triaging any diff against it

# The dispatch tier's load harness (blueprint/testing.md, blueprint/deploy.md).
# Never a PR gate: it is a load generator, and the only thing it can be pointed
# at is a loopback stack this job stands up, or staging behind the `staging`
# environment's approval. The harness crate's own unit tests block merges in
# CI's `Cargo Check & Test (Linux)` job.
name: Load Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Target'
        required: true
        default: 'local'
        type: choice
        options:
          - local
          - staging
      scenario:
        description: 'Scenario'
        required: true
        default: 'mixed'
        type: choice
        options:
          - content-ingest
          - gateway-read
          - name-wave
          - mixed
          - byo-advisory
      clients:
        description: 'Concurrent accounts (staging caps at 8)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      ops_per_client:
        description: 'Iterations per account (staging caps at 50)'
        required: false
        default: '20'
      block_bytes:
        description: 'Upload block size in bytes, max 2 MiB'
        required: false
        default: '65536'
      batch_size:
        description: 'Registry batch size, max 1000'
        required: false
        default: '25'
      ramp_ms:
        description: 'Per-client start stagger in ms; 0 is a spike'
        required: false
        default: '0'

# Two runs against the same target would measure each other. Queue rather than
# cancel, so a staging run already loading the 2-vCPU box finishes cleanly.
concurrency:
  group: load-test-${{ inputs.environment }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions: {}

jobs:
  load-test:
    name: 'Load Test: ${{ inputs.scenario }} on ${{ inputs.environment }}'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: ${{ inputs.environment == 'staging' && 'staging' || '' }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_load
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s

    env:
      SCENARIO: ${{ inputs.scenario }}
      CLIENTS: ${{ inputs.clients }}
      OPS_PER_CLIENT: ${{ inputs.ops_per_client }}
      BLOCK_BYTES: ${{ inputs.block_bytes }}
      BATCH_SIZE: ${{ inputs.batch_size }}
      RAMP_MS: ${{ inputs.ramp_ms }}
      TARGET: ${{ inputs.environment }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: linux-cargo-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: linux-cargo-

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: inputs.environment == 'local'
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Stand up the local API over the CI stack
        if: inputs.environment == 'local'
        env:
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_load
          NODE_ENV: test
          JWT_SECRET: load-harness-jwt-secret
          KUBO_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: load-harness-secret
          # A whole run provisions its accounts from one IP, so the per-IP auth
          # bucket would cap how many virtual clients can exist. Honored only on
          # an undeployed profile (apps/api/src/ops/throttling.ts).
          THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT: '500'
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build
          node apps/api/dist/main.js > /tmp/api.log 2>&1 &
          curl -fsS --retry 60 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1 http://localhost:3000/health \
            || { echo '--- API log ---'; cat /tmp/api.log; exit 1; }

      # The harness defaults its own loopback URLs, so a local run only needs
      # the shared test-login secret.
      - name: Resolve the target
        env:
          STAGING_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
          STAGING_GATEWAY_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_GATEWAY_URL }}
          STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET }}
          STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ "$TARGET" = 'staging' ]; then
            if [ -z "$STAGING_API_URL" ] || [ -z "$STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET" ]; then
              echo '::error::staging runs need the STAGING_API_URL variable and STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET secret'
              exit 1
            fi
            if [ "$SCENARIO" = 'gateway-read' ] && [ -z "$STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN" ]; then
              echo '::error::gateway-read on staging needs the STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN secret; the read accelerator is behind forward_auth'
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "LOAD_TEST_API_URL=$STAGING_API_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_URL=$STAGING_GATEWAY_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_SECRET=$STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN=$STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          else
            echo 'LOAD_TEST_SECRET=load-harness-secret' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      # The harness refuses a target the flags and the environment disagree
      # about: `local` only ever reaches loopback and `staging` only ever reaches
      # a non-loopback https URL, so a mis-dispatched run fails before it loads
      # anything. Bounds on clients/ops are enforced per target too.
      - name: Run the load harness

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# The dispatch tier's load harness (blueprint/testing.md, blueprint/deploy.md).
# Never a PR gate: it is a load generator, and the only thing it can be pointed
# at is a loopback stack this job stands up, or staging behind the `staging`
# environment's approval. The harness crate's own unit tests block merges in
# CI's `Cargo Check & Test (Linux)` job.
name: Load Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Target'
        required: true
        default: 'local'
        type: choice
        options:
          - local
          - staging
      scenario:
        description: 'Scenario'
        required: true
        default: 'mixed'
        type: choice
        options:
          - content-ingest
          - gateway-read
          - name-wave
          - mixed
          - byo-advisory
      clients:
        description: 'Concurrent accounts (staging caps at 8)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      ops_per_client:
        description: 'Iterations per account (staging caps at 50)'
        required: false
        default: '20'
      block_bytes:
        description: 'Upload block size in bytes, max 2 MiB'
        required: false
        default: '65536'
      batch_size:
        description: 'Registry batch size, max 1000'
        required: false
        default: '25'
      ramp_ms:
        description: 'Per-client start stagger in ms; 0 is a spike'
        required: false
        default: '0'

# Two runs against the same target would measure each other. Queue rather than
# cancel, so a staging run already loading the 2-vCPU box finishes cleanly.
concurrency:
  group: load-test-${{ inputs.environment }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions: {}

jobs:
  load-test:
    name: 'Load Test: ${{ inputs.scenario }} on ${{ inputs.environment }}'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: ${{ inputs.environment == 'staging' && 'staging' || '' }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_load
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s

    env:
      SCENARIO: ${{ inputs.scenario }}
      CLIENTS: ${{ inputs.clients }}
      OPS_PER_CLIENT: ${{ inputs.ops_per_client }}
      BLOCK_BYTES: ${{ inputs.block_bytes }}
      BATCH_SIZE: ${{ inputs.batch_size }}
      RAMP_MS: ${{ inputs.ramp_ms }}
      TARGET: ${{ inputs.environment }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: linux-cargo-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: linux-cargo-

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: inputs.environment == 'local'
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Stand up the local API over the CI stack
        if: inputs.environment == 'local'
        env:
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_load
          NODE_ENV: test
          JWT_SECRET: load-harness-jwt-secret
          KUBO_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: load-harness-secret
          # A whole run provisions its accounts from one IP, so the per-IP auth
          # bucket would cap how many virtual clients can exist. Honored only on
          # an undeployed profile (apps/api/src/ops/throttling.ts).
          THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT: '500'
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build
          node apps/api/dist/main.js > /tmp/api.log 2>&1 &
          curl -fsS --retry 60 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1 http://localhost:3000/health \
            || { echo '--- API log ---'; cat /tmp/api.log; exit 1; }

      # The harness defaults its own loopback URLs, so a local run only needs
      # the shared test-login secret.
      - name: Resolve the target
        env:
          API_URL: ${{ vars.API_URL }}
          STAGING_GATEWAY_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_GATEWAY_URL }}
          STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET }}
          STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ "$TARGET" = 'staging' ]; then
            if [ -z "$API_URL" ] || [ -z "$STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET" ]; then
              echo '::error::staging runs need the API_URL variable and STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET secret'
              exit 1
            fi
            if [ "$SCENARIO" = 'gateway-read' ] && [ -z "$STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN" ]; then
              echo '::error::gateway-read on staging needs the STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN secret; the read accelerator is behind forward_auth'
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "LOAD_TEST_API_URL=$STAGING_API_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_URL=$STAGING_GATEWAY_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_SECRET=$STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN=$STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          else
            echo 'LOAD_TEST_SECRET=load-harness-secret' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      # The harness refuses a target the flags and the environment disagree
      # about: `local` only ever reaches loopback and `staging` only ever reaches
      # a non-loopback https URL, so a mis-dispatched run fails before it loads
      # anything. Bounds on clients/ops are enforced per target too.
      - name: Run the load harness
        run: |
          cargo run --release -p cipherbox-load -- \
            --scenario "$SCENARIO" \
            --target "$TARGET" \
            --clients "$CLIENTS" \
            --ops-per-client "$OPS_PER_CLIENT" \
            --block-bytes "$BLOCK_BYTES" \
            --batch-size "$BATCH_SIZE" \
            --ramp-ms "$RAMP_MS"

      - name: Upload the metrics report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: load-metrics-${{ inputs.scenario }}-${{ inputs.environment }}
          path: load-reports/*.json
          retention-days: 30
          if-no-files-found: warn

1	<!-- generated-by: gsd-doc-writer -->

3	# Deployment
4	
5	> **v1 document — partially superseded.** This describes the v1 pipeline as of the freeze (`v1-freeze`, branch `v1`). The v2 scheme is normative in `blueprint/deploy.md` ([FSM1/cipher-box-next](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next)): single product version, single-component release-please (dormant, dispatch-only during the build); `pr-release-preview.yml`, `release-gate.yml`, and `cargo-lock-release-sync.yml` are deleted. The staging-tag flow and VPS mechanics below still describe the live setup until the v2 cutover; this document will be rewritten during the v2 build.
6	
7	This document covers the release pipeline, staging deployment, TEE worker deployment, desktop app packaging, and landing page deployment for CipherBox.
8	
9	## Release Pipeline (Release Please)
10	
11	CipherBox uses [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please) for automated changelog generation, version bumping, and GitHub Release creation. Configuration is in `release-please-config.json` and version state is tracked in `.release-please-manifest.json`.
12	
13	### How it works
14	
15	On every push to `main`, the `release-please.yml` workflow runs and creates or updates a release PR accumulating conventional commits. When the release PR is merged, Release Please:
16	
17	1. Bumps each changed package's version in its manifest file
18	2. Updates `CHANGELOG.md` entries
19	3. Creates a GitHub Release with a component-scoped tag
20	
21	### Versioned packages
22	
23	All packages use `include-component-in-tag: true` and `bump-minor-pre-major: true`. Tags follow the pattern `{component}-v{version}`.
24	
25	| Package path          | Component tag prefix      | Release type |
26	| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------ |
27	| `.` (root)            | `cipher-box-v`            | node         |
28	| `apps/api`            | `@cipherbox/api-v`        | node         |
29	| `apps/web`            | `@cipherbox/web-v`        | node         |
30	| `apps/desktop`        | `cipherbox-desktop-v`     | node         |
31	| `apps/tee-worker`     | `cipherbox-tee-worker-v`  | node         |
32	| `packages/core`       | `@cipherbox/core-v`       | node         |
33	| `packages/crypto`     | `@cipherbox/crypto-v`     | node         |
34	| `packages/api-client` | `@cipherbox/api-client-v` | node         |
35	| `packages/sdk-core`   | `@cipherbox/sdk-core-v`   | node         |
36	| `packages/sdk`        | `@cipherbox/sdk-v`        | node         |
37	| `crates/crypto`       | `cipherbox-crypto-v`      | rust         |
38	| `crates/core`         | `cipherbox-core-v`        | rust         |
39	| `crates/api-client`   | `cipherbox-api-client-v`  | rust         |
40	| `crates/fuse`         | `cipherbox-fuse-v`        | rust         |
41	| `crates/sdk`          | `cipherbox-sdk-v`         | rust         |
42	
43	For `apps/desktop`, Release Please additionally propagates the version to `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` and `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` via the `extra-files` config.
44	
45	### Release PR title pattern
46	
47	```text
48	chore: release v${version}
49	```
50	
51	### Latest release flag
52	
53	After creating all batch releases, the `release-please.yml` workflow clears the "latest" flag from every release it creates. The desktop release workflow (`desktop-staging-release.yml`) marks the desktop release as latest so that `/releases/latest/` resolves to the desktop download (used by the Tauri auto-updater).
54	
55	### Release gate (E2E prerequisite)
56	
57	Before a release PR can be merged, the `release-gate.yml` workflow verifies that E2E tests have passed on the current `main` HEAD:
58	
59	- Detects which packages changed (web/desktop path patterns) since the previous release tag
60	- Polls the `ci-e2e.yml` workflow run to confirm Web E2E and/or Desktop E2E passed
61	- Falls back to the most recent CI E2E run where those tests actually executed
62	
63	## Staging Deployment
64	
65	### Triggering a staging deploy
66	
67	Staging deploys are triggered manually via the `tag-staging.yml` workflow (workflow dispatch in GitHub Actions). The workflow:
68	
69	1. Resolves the current `main` HEAD SHA
70	2. Verifies that `main` HEAD carries a release tag (pattern: `cipher-box-v*`, `cipherbox-*-v*`, or `@cipherbox/*`) — you must wait for a release-please PR to merge before tagging staging
71	3. Runs Web E2E (`web-e2e.yml`) and Desktop E2E (`desktop-e2e.yml`) against the resolved SHA in parallel
72	4. Requires `staging-approval` environment approval
73	5. Creates a tag of the form `staging-YYYYMMDD-release-N` (N is a per-day sequential counter) and pushes it
74	6. Calls `deploy-staging.yml` as a reusable workflow
75	
76	The `staging-` prefix avoids collision with release-please tag patterns.
77	
78	### Deploy workflow (`deploy-staging.yml`)
79	
80	Triggered by `staging-*` tag pushes or by `tag-staging.yml` via `workflow_call`. The workflow runs these jobs in parallel then converges:
81	
82	- **Build & Push API Image** — builds `apps/api/Dockerfile` from repo root, pushes to `ghcr.io/{owner}/cipherbox-api` with three tags: `{api-version}`, `latest-staging`, `{staging-tag}`
83	- **Build & Push TEE Worker Image** — builds `apps/tee-worker/Dockerfile` from repo root, pushes to `ghcr.io/{owner}/cipherbox-tee-worker` with the same tagging scheme
84	- **Build Web App** — installs deps, builds shared packages, then builds `@cipherbox/web` with staging env vars injected at build time; uploads `apps/web/dist/` as a workflow artifact
85	- **Build Desktop App (macOS / Windows / Linux)** — see [Desktop App Packaging](#desktop-app-packaging) below
86	- **Deploy to Staging VPS** — waits for the three build jobs above, then SCPs files to the VPS and runs Docker Compose (see [VPS Deployment](#vps-deployment))
87	- **Provision Grafana Dashboard** — waits for VPS deploy, then pushes `docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json` to Grafana Cloud
88	
89	### VPS deployment
90	
91	The `deploy-vps` job:
92	
93	1. Downloads the web dist artifact
94	2. Generates `.env.staging` from GitHub Actions secrets/vars and appends image tags and component versions
95	3. SCPs `.env.staging`, `docker/docker-compose.staging.yml`, `docker/Caddyfile`, and `docker/alloy-config.river` to `/opt/cipherbox/` on the staging VPS <!-- VERIFY: VPS host address is in the HOST variable -->
96	4. Copies the web dist to `/opt/cipherbox/web/` (with `rm: true` to replace previous dist)
97	5. On the VPS: logs in to GHCR, pulls new images, runs database migrations (`node dist/run-migrations.js`), brings services up with `docker compose up -d`, restarts Caddy, and prunes old images
98	
99	### Docker Compose services (staging)
100	
101	Configuration: `docker/docker-compose.staging.yml`
102	
103	| Service      | Image                                        | Description                                                                                                                              |
104	| ------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
105	| `api`        | `ghcr.io/{owner}/cipherbox-api:{tag}`        | NestJS API, port 3000 (loopback only)                                                                                                    |
106	| `postgres`   | `postgres:16-alpine`                         | PostgreSQL database, port 5432 (loopback only)                                                                                           |
107	| `redis`      | `redis:7-alpine`                             | Redis (password-protected), port 6379 (loopback only)                                                                                    |
108	| `ipfs`       | `ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0`                          | Kubo IPFS node (pebbleds profile), p2p port 4001 public, API/gateway loopback                                                            |

## What this lands

Drops the `STAGING_` prefix from the four GitHub Actions **variables**. They are scoped to the
`staging` environment, so the prefix restates the scope and goes stale the moment a production
environment exists.

| Was | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `vars.STAGING_API_URL` | `vars.API_URL` |
| `vars.STAGING_HOST` | `vars.HOST` |
| `vars.STAGING_USER` | `vars.USER` |
| `vars.STAGING_DB_USERNAME` | `vars.DB_USERNAME` |

The new variables are already created in the `staging` environment with values copied from the old
ones and verified by read-back. **The old variables are still present**, so this branch and `main`
both work; they are deleted after this merges.

## Why unprefixed `HOST` and `USER` are safe here

A bare `USER` in a workflow `env:` block would shadow the shell's own `$USER`. Every usage here is
an inline `${{ vars.X }}` interpolated into an action input (`host:`, `username:`) or a heredoc
line — **none goes through a workflow `env:` key**, so nothing is shadowed. Worth remembering if a
future step does put one in `env:`.

## Scope check

Every job that reads these declares `environment: staging`, so the variables resolve:

- `deploy-staging.yml` — `build-web`, `build-desktop`, `build-desktop-windows`, `build-desktop-linux`, `deploy-vps`
- `desktop-staging-release.yml` — all three build jobs
- `deploy-landing.yml` — `build-and-deploy`
- `load-test.yml` — `load-test`, whose `environment:` is conditional on the staging target

## Not in scope — the secrets

Seven `STAGING_`-prefixed **secrets** remain: `STAGING_DB_PASSWORD`, `STAGING_JWT_SECRET`,
`STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD`, `STAGING_SSH_KEY`, `STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET`,
`STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, `STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET`.

Secret values are write-only over the API, so they cannot be copied to a new name programmatically —
each has to be re-entered by hand. Renaming them is a separate, human-driven change.

## Unrelated finding

`load-test.yml:154` reads `vars.STAGING_GATEWAY_URL`, which **is not defined at any scope**. The
guard immediately below it checks only `API_URL` and `STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, so a `gateway-read`
scenario against staging would run with an empty gateway URL rather than failing fast. Left alone
here — it is a real bug, not a rename.

## Gates run locally

YAML parse on all four changed workflows, `markdownlint-cli2 docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`,
`node scripts/check-tracker-refs.mjs`, and a repo-wide grep confirming zero remaining references to
any of the four old names.

`FSM1/cipher-box` splits Actions variables across two scopes, and `gh variable list` (repo scope)
shows only 5 of them — it is NOT the full picture.

  variable that web-e2e needs must be set at **repo** scope or it silently reads empty.

`deployEnvGate()` throws when `missingDeployEnv()` is non-empty, and that fires only for

commit, not a runtime bug. Verify by running the real build both ways before merging:

missing variable, so one negative-control run also proves the *others* resolve.

That value is v1's hardcoded verifier (`docs/AUTHENTICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.1; the API signs its

---
name: project-staging-build-vars-live-at-environment-scope
description: "CipherBox staging deploy vars live at the `staging` GitHub environment scope, not repo scope — but web-e2e declares no environment and only sees repo scope"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 80d330f6-bcef-42f9-92ad-b3f2dc8fe04e
  modified: 2026-08-04T21:48:40.078Z
---

`FSM1/cipher-box` splits Actions variables across two scopes, and `gh variable list` (repo scope)
shows only 5 of them — it is NOT the full picture.

- **`staging` environment scope (15 vars)** — `STAGING_API_URL`, `STAGING_HOST`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`,
  `CLOUDFLARE_*`, `GRAFANA_*`, `PHALA_TEE_WORKER_URL`, … Every staging build job
  (`deploy-staging.yml` `build-web` + `build-desktop-{macos,windows,linux}`, and all of
  `desktop-staging-release.yml`) declares `environment: staging`, so it sees repo vars *and* these.
- **Repo scope (5 vars)** — `VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER`, `GRAFANA_DS_*`,
  `GRAFANA_URL`, `RELEASE_BOT_APP_ID`. There is no org-level variable set (404).
- **`web-e2e.yml` declares NO `environment:`** — so it sees repo scope ONLY. A `VITE_*` build
  variable that web-e2e needs must be set at **repo** scope or it silently reads empty.

**Why to check this before merging a build-time env gate:** `apps/web/vite.config.ts`'s
`deployEnvGate()` throws when `missingDeployEnv()` is non-empty, and that fires only for
`VITE_ENVIRONMENT` of `staging`/`production`. An unset variable is a red staging deploy on the merge
commit, not a runtime bug. Verify by running the real build both ways before merging:

```
VITE_ENVIRONMENT=staging VITE_API_URL=… VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID=… \
  pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build:bundle
```

Unset → `Error: a staging build cannot log in without <NAME>`; set → exit 0. The error names every
missing variable, so one negative-control run also proves the *others* resolve.

`VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER = cipherbox-identity` was set at repo scope 2026-08-04 to unblock #1035.
That value is v1's hardcoded verifier (`docs/AUTHENTICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.1; the API signs its
JWT with `kid: cipherbox-identity-1`), and staging is DEVNET on the same client ID.

See [[project-v1-staging-only-devnet.md]] and [[project-ci-excludes-web-unit-tests]].
