Done — **PR #1113** (draft): `chore(ci): drop the STAGING_ prefix from the deploy environment variables`.

## First, a correction

I told you `vars.STAGING_API_URL` didn't exist at any scope. **That was wrong.** It was in the `staging` environment all along. My check missed it because the environments-variables API paginates at 10 without saying so, and there were 15 — `STAGING_API_URL` sorts past the cut. That false negative made it into both the wave-5 handoff and the wave-6 plan; both are fixed, and the memory now says to pass `per_page=100` and compare `.total_count` against the row count.

## What changed

Four variables renamed, values copied and verified by read-back:

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `STAGING_API_URL` | `API_URL` |
| `STAGING_HOST` | `HOST` |
| `STAGING_USER` | `USER` |
| `STAGING_DB_USERNAME` | `DB_USERNAME` |

19 references updated across `deploy-staging.yml`, `desktop-staging-release.yml`, `deploy-landing.yml`, `load-test.yml`, and the `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` table. Repo-wide grep confirms zero remaining references to any old name.

**The old variables still exist**, so `main` and the branch both work. Delete them after the PR merges — tell me when and I'll do it.

I checked one thing before committing to bare `HOST`/`USER`: a bare `USER` in a workflow `env:` block would shadow the shell's own. Every usage here is an inline `${{ vars.X }}` into an action input (`host:`, `username:`) or a heredoc line — none goes through an `env:` key, so nothing is shadowed. Worth remembering if a future step does put one in `env:`.

## The secrets can't be done this way

Seven `STAGING_`-prefixed secrets remain: `STAGING_DB_PASSWORD`, `STAGING_JWT_SECRET`, `STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD`, `STAGING_SSH_KEY`, `STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET`, `STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, `STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET`.

Secret values are write-only over the API — there's no read to copy from, so a rename means re-entering each value by hand. I can prepare the workflow-side rename in a follow-up PR so you only have to paste the values into `gh secret set`, if that's useful.

## One thing I found while in there

`load-test.yml:154` reads `vars.STAGING_GATEWAY_URL`, which **isn't defined at any scope** — and this time I checked with pagination. The guard two lines below only validates `API_URL` and `STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, so a `gateway-read` scenario against staging would run with an empty gateway URL instead of failing fast. I left it alone since it's a bug rather than a rename; it's flagged in the PR body.

content.text:
Short answer: **no.** GitHub Actions secrets are write-only — there's no read endpoint on the API or the UI, by design. The only way a value comes back out is to echo it from a workflow that has access, and GitHub masks secrets in logs; getting around the masking means deliberately writing your own credentials into retained CI logs. Not worth it for seven staging values you can just rotate.

But "generate and set" isn't uniformly safe — some of these have a counterpart outside GitHub. Let me check how each is consumed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Rotate the staging environment's Actions secrets onto unprefixed names.
#
# GitHub secrets are write-only: there is no API or UI read, so an existing value
# cannot be copied to a new name. Renaming a secret therefore means minting a new
# value, which is only safe when nothing outside GitHub already knows the old one.
#
# Two of the seven have a counterpart on the VPS and are refused by default:
# rotating them in GitHub alone breaks staging until the paired change lands.
#
#   ./scripts/rotate-staging-secrets.sh              # dry run, prints the plan
#   ./scripts/rotate-staging-secrets.sh --apply      # rotate the safe set
#   ./scripts/rotate-staging-secrets.sh --apply --include-db
#
set -euo pipefail

REPO="FSM1/cipher-box"
ENVIRONMENT="staging"
APPLY=0
INCLUDE_DB=0

# Rotating these only rewrites .env.staging, which every deploy regenerates and
# every container re-reads on restart. No state outside GitHub knows the old value.
SAFE_ROTATIONS=(
  "STAGING_JWT_SECRET:JWT_SECRET:base64"
  "STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET:TEST_LOGIN_SECRET:base64"
  "STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET:THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET:base64"
  "STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD:REDIS_PASSWORD:base64"
  "STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET:TEE_WORKER_SECRET:hex"
)

usage() {
  sed -n '2,15p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  cat <<'TXT'

Refused without an explicit flag:

  STAGING_DB_PASSWORD    Postgres applies POSTGRES_PASSWORD only when it
                         initialises an empty data volume. The staging volume
                         already exists, so a new secret makes the API's
                         DB_PASSWORD disagree with the live role and every
                         connection fails. Pair it with, on the VPS:
                           docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml exec postgres \
                             psql -U "$DB_USERNAME" -d cipherbox_staging \
                             -c "ALTER USER \"$DB_USERNAME\" WITH PASSWORD '<new>';"
                         Then set the secret. Pass --include-db to have this
                         script print the new value once so you can do both.

  STAGING_SSH_KEY        This is the deploy key. Minting a new one without first
                         installing its public half in the VPS authorized_keys
                         locks the pipeline out of the box it deploys to, and
                         this script cannot verify the VPS side. Rotate by hand:
                           ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'cipherbox staging deploy' -f ./k
                           ssh-copy-id -i ./k.pub <user>@<host>   # verify a login
                           gh secret set SSH_KEY --env staging --repo FSM1/cipher-box < ./k
                           shred -u ./k ./k.pub
                         Never leave the private half on disk afterwards.
TXT
}

for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --apply) APPLY=1 ;;
    --include-db) INCLUDE_DB=1 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown argument: $arg" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

command -v gh >/dev/null || { echo "gh is not installed" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v openssl >/dev/null || { echo "openssl is not installed" >&2; exit 1; }
GH=(env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh)

"${GH[@]}" api "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENVIRONMENT" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || { echo "cannot reach the $ENVIRONMENT environment on $REPO" >&2; exit 1; }

generate() {
  case "$1" in
    base64) openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '\n' ;;
    hex) openssl rand -hex 32 | tr -d '\n' ;;
  esac
}

secret_exists() {
  "${GH[@]}" api "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENVIRONMENT/secrets/$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

updated_at() {
  "${GH[@]}" api "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENVIRONMENT/secrets/$1" --jq '.updated_at' 2>/dev/null
}

rotate() {
  local old="$1" new="$2" kind="$3" reveal="${4:-0}"

  if [ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ]; then
    printf '  would rotate  %-32s -> %-24s (%s)\n' "$old" "$new" "$kind"
    return 0
  fi

  local before value
  before="$(updated_at "$new" || true)"
  value="$(generate "$kind")"

  # Piped, never --body: an argument would be visible in the process list.
  printf '%s' "$value" | "${GH[@]}" secret set "$new" --env "$ENVIRONMENT" --repo "$REPO" >/dev/null

  local after
  after="$(updated_at "$new" || true)"
  if [ -z "$after" ] || { [ -n "$before" ] && [ "$before" = "$after" ]; }; then
    echo "  FAILED        $new (no write recorded)" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  printf '  rotated       %-32s -> %-24s @ %s\n' "$old" "$new" "$after"

  if [ "$reveal" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo
    echo "  The paired VPS change needs this value. It is shown once and not stored:"
    echo "    $value"
    echo
  fi
  unset value
}

echo "Repo $REPO, environment $ENVIRONMENT"
[ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ] && echo "DRY RUN — nothing is written. Re-run with --apply."
echo

FAILED=0
for row in "${SAFE_ROTATIONS[@]}"; do
  IFS=: read -r old new kind <<<"$row"
  secret_exists "$old" || printf '  note: %s does not exist; %s is being created fresh\n' "$old" "$new"
  rotate "$old" "$new" "$kind" || FAILED=1
done

if [ "$INCLUDE_DB" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo
  echo "DB_PASSWORD: staging is broken between this write and the ALTER USER on the VPS."
  rotate STAGING_DB_PASSWORD DB_PASSWORD base64 1 || FAILED=1
else
  echo
  echo "  skipped       STAGING_DB_PASSWORD  (needs a paired ALTER USER; --include-db)"
fi
echo "  skipped       STAGING_SSH_KEY      (rotate by hand; see --help)"

if [ "$APPLY" -eq 1 ] && [ "$FAILED" -eq 0 ]; then
  cat <<TXT

Next, in order:
  1. Update every workflow reference from secrets.STAGING_<NAME> to secrets.<NAME>.
  2. REDIS_PASSWORD and TEE_WORKER_SECRET are referenced by
     docker/docker-compose.staging.yml but were never written into .env.staging,
     so staging redis has been running with an empty requirepass. Add both lines
     to the generator in .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml.
  3. Merge, run a staging deploy, confirm it is healthy.
  4. Only then delete the old secrets:
       for s in STAGING_JWT_SECRET STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET \\
                STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD \\
                STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET; do
         env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh secret delete "\$s" --env $ENVIRONMENT --repo $REPO
       done
TXT
fi

exit "$FAILED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Rotate the staging environment's Actions secrets onto unprefixed names.
#
# GitHub secrets are write-only: there is no API or UI read, so an existing value
# cannot be copied to a new name. Renaming a secret therefore means minting a new
# value, which is only safe when nothing outside GitHub already knows the old one.
#
# Two of the seven have a counterpart on the VPS and are refused by default:
# rotating them in GitHub alone breaks staging until the paired change lands.
#
#   ./scripts/rotate-staging-secrets.sh              # dry run, prints the plan
#   ./scripts/rotate-staging-secrets.sh --apply      # rotate the safe set
#   ./scripts/rotate-staging-secrets.sh --apply --include-db
#
set -euo pipefail

REPO="FSM1/cipher-box"
ENVIRONMENT="staging"
APPLY=0
INCLUDE_DB=0

# Rotating these only rewrites .env.staging, which every deploy regenerates and
# every container re-reads on restart. No state outside GitHub knows the old value.
SAFE_ROTATIONS=(
  "STAGING_JWT_SECRET:JWT_SECRET:base64"
  "STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET:TEST_LOGIN_SECRET:base64"
  "STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET:THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET:base64"
  "STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD:REDIS_PASSWORD:base64"
)

# v2 has no TEE (AGENTS.md: the republisher is a keyless re-PUT module inside the
# API), so this one is deleted rather than rotated onto a new name.
RETIRED=("STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET")

usage() {
  sed -n '2,15p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  cat <<'TXT'

Refused without an explicit flag:

  STAGING_DB_PASSWORD    Postgres applies POSTGRES_PASSWORD only when it
                         initialises an empty data volume. The staging volume
                         already exists, so a new secret makes the API's
                         DB_PASSWORD disagree with the live role and every
                         connection fails. Pair it with, on the VPS:
                           docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml exec postgres \
                             psql -U "$DB_USERNAME" -d cipherbox_staging \
                             -c "ALTER USER \"$DB_USERNAME\" WITH PASSWORD '<new>';"
                         Then set the secret. Pass --include-db to have this
                         script print the new value once so you can do both.

  STAGING_SSH_KEY        This is the deploy key. Minting a new one without first
                         installing its public half in the VPS authorized_keys
                         locks the pipeline out of the box it deploys to, and
                         this script cannot verify the VPS side. Rotate by hand:
                           ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'cipherbox staging deploy' -f ./k
                           ssh-copy-id -i ./k.pub <user>@<host>   # verify a login
                           gh secret set SSH_KEY --env staging --repo FSM1/cipher-box < ./k
                           shred -u ./k ./k.pub
                         Never leave the private half on disk afterwards.
TXT
}

for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --apply) APPLY=1 ;;
    --include-db) INCLUDE_DB=1 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown argument: $arg" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

command -v gh >/dev/null || { echo "gh is not installed" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v openssl >/dev/null || { echo "openssl is not installed" >&2; exit 1; }
GH=(env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh)

"${GH[@]}" api "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENVIRONMENT" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || { echo "cannot reach the $ENVIRONMENT environment on $REPO" >&2; exit 1; }

generate() {
  case "$1" in
    base64) openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '\n' ;;
    hex) openssl rand -hex 32 | tr -d '\n' ;;
  esac
}

secret_exists() {
  "${GH[@]}" api "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENVIRONMENT/secrets/$1" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

updated_at() {
  "${GH[@]}" api "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENVIRONMENT/secrets/$1" --jq '.updated_at' 2>/dev/null
}

rotate() {
  local old="$1" new="$2" kind="$3" reveal="${4:-0}"

  if [ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ]; then
    printf '  would rotate  %-32s -> %-24s (%s)\n' "$old" "$new" "$kind"

    return 1

    echo "    $value"
    echo
  fi

}

echo

for row in "${SAFE_ROTATIONS[@]}"; do

fi
echo "  skipped       STAGING_SSH_KEY      (rotate by hand; see --help)"

Next, in order:

       done

fi

content.text:
**No — there's no way to read a GitHub secret back.** Write-only on both the API and the UI, by design. The only route out is echoing one from a workflow, and GitHub masks secrets in logs, so it means deliberately defeating the masking to write your own credentials into retained CI logs. Not worth it for seven staging values. Generate-and-set is the right call.

`scripts/rotate-staging-secrets.sh` is written and dry-run clean. But **not all seven are free to rotate**, so it refuses two by default:

```
  would rotate  STAGING_JWT_SECRET             -> JWT_SECRET
  would rotate  STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET      -> TEST_LOGIN_SECRET
  would rotate  STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET -> THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET
  would rotate  STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD         -> REDIS_PASSWORD
  would delete  STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET      (v2 has no TEE)
  skipped       STAGING_DB_PASSWORD  (needs a paired ALTER USER; --include-db)
  skipped       STAGING_SSH_KEY      (rotate by hand; see --help)
```

**`DB_PASSWORD`** — Postgres applies `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` only when it initialises an *empty* data volume. Staging's volume already exists, so a new secret just makes the API disagree with the live role and every connection fails. It needs a paired `ALTER USER` on the VPS; `--include-db` prints the value once so you can do both.

**`SSH_KEY`** — that's the deploy key. Minting a new one without first installing the public half in the VPS `authorized_keys` locks the pipeline out of the box it deploys to, and the script can't verify the VPS side. `--help` has the by-hand sequence, ending in `shred -u`.

The script pipes values via stdin rather than `--body` so they never appear in the process list, and verifies each write by comparing `updated_at` before and after.

## Redis — I need you to confirm, because the evidence points the other way

You said REDIS_PASSWORD should definitely be present. I wired it, but I think it may be wrong, and it's cheap to check now versus after a deploy:

- **`deploy-staging.yml:1-4` says so itself**: *"the tee-worker image build, **redis**, and SendGrid plumbing are gone with the v1 layout."*
- **`apps/api` has no redis anything** — no `redis`/`ioredis` dependency, no `REDIS_*` env var, zero source references. `@nestjs/throttler` v6 is installed but with no redis storage adapter, so it's in-memory.
- `.env.staging` stopped emitting `REDIS_PASSWORD` deliberately, as part of that v1 removal.

So `docker-compose.staging.yml` still declaring a redis service looks like stale v1 residue rather than the workflow being wrong — and on a 2-vCPU staging box, an unused redis is memory that someguy could use.

**1.** Delete the redis service from compose (my recommendation), drop `REDIS_PASSWORD` from the script, delete `STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD`.
**2.** Keep redis and wire `REDIS_PASSWORD` into `.env.staging` — correct if you're planning a v2 use I can't see, e.g. throttler storage once the API runs more than one instance.

Tell me which and I'll finish it in one pass.

The TEE side is unambiguous and I've handled it: `apps/tee-worker` has **zero tracked files** — already deleted — yet compose still declares a `tee-worker` service pulling `cipherbox-tee-worker:${TAG}`, an image nothing builds any more. That service needs removing from compose along with the secret, or the next staging deploy tries to pull a nonexistent image. I've held that edit only because it's the same file as the redis decision.

# The dispatch tier's load harness (blueprint/testing.md, blueprint/deploy.md).
# Never a PR gate: it is a load generator, and the only thing it can be pointed
# at is a loopback stack this job stands up, or staging behind the `staging`
# environment's approval. The harness crate's own unit tests block merges in
# CI's `Cargo Check & Test (Linux)` job.
name: Load Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Target'
        required: true
        default: 'local'
        type: choice
        options:
          - local
          - staging
      scenario:
        description: 'Scenario'
        required: true
        default: 'mixed'
        type: choice
        options:
          - content-ingest
          - gateway-read
          - name-wave
          - mixed
          - byo-advisory
      clients:
        description: 'Concurrent accounts (staging caps at 8)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      ops_per_client:
        description: 'Iterations per account (staging caps at 50)'
        required: false
        default: '20'
      block_bytes:
        description: 'Upload block size in bytes, max 2 MiB'
        required: false
        default: '65536'
      batch_size:
        description: 'Registry batch size, max 1000'
        required: false
        default: '25'
      ramp_ms:
        description: 'Per-client start stagger in ms; 0 is a spike'
        required: false
        default: '0'

# Two runs against the same target would measure each other. Queue rather than
# cancel, so a staging run already loading the 2-vCPU box finishes cleanly.
concurrency:
  group: load-test-${{ inputs.environment }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions: {}

jobs:
  load-test:
    name: 'Load Test: ${{ inputs.scenario }} on ${{ inputs.environment }}'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: ${{ inputs.environment == 'staging' && 'staging' || '' }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_load
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s

    env:
      SCENARIO: ${{ inputs.scenario }}
      CLIENTS: ${{ inputs.clients }}
      OPS_PER_CLIENT: ${{ inputs.ops_per_client }}
      BLOCK_BYTES: ${{ inputs.block_bytes }}
      BATCH_SIZE: ${{ inputs.batch_size }}
      RAMP_MS: ${{ inputs.ramp_ms }}
      TARGET: ${{ inputs.environment }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: linux-cargo-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: linux-cargo-

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: inputs.environment == 'local'
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Stand up the local API over the CI stack
        if: inputs.environment == 'local'
        env:
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_load
          NODE_ENV: test
          JWT_SECRET: load-harness-jwt-secret
          KUBO_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: load-harness-secret
          # A whole run provisions its accounts from one IP, so the per-IP auth
          # bucket would cap how many virtual clients can exist. Honored only on
          # an undeployed profile (apps/api/src/ops/throttling.ts).
          THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT: '500'
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build
          node apps/api/dist/main.js > /tmp/api.log 2>&1 &
          curl -fsS --retry 60 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1 http://localhost:3000/health \
            || { echo '--- API log ---'; cat /tmp/api.log; exit 1; }

      # The harness defaults its own loopback URLs, so a local run only needs
      # the shared test-login secret.
      - name: Resolve the target
        env:
          API_URL: ${{ vars.API_URL }}
          IPFS_GATEWAY_URL: ${{ vars.IPFS_GATEWAY_URL }}
          STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET }}
          STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ "$TARGET" = 'staging' ]; then
            if [ -z "$API_URL" ] || [ -z "$STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET" ]; then
              echo '::error::staging runs need the API_URL variable and STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET secret'
              exit 1
            fi
            if [ "$SCENARIO" = 'gateway-read' ] && [ -z "$STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN" ]; then
              echo '::error::gateway-read on staging needs the STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN secret; the read accelerator is behind forward_auth'
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "LOAD_TEST_API_URL=$API_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_URL=$IPFS_GATEWAY_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_SECRET=$STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN=$STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          else
            echo 'LOAD_TEST_SECRET=load-harness-secret' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      # The harness refuses a target the flags and the environment disagree
      # about: `local` only ever reaches loopback and `staging` only ever reaches
      # a non-loopback https URL, so a mis-dispatched run fails before it loads
      # anything. Bounds on clients/ops are enforced per target too.
      - name: Run the load harness
        run: |
          cargo run --release -p cipherbox-load -- \
            --scenario "$SCENARIO" \
            --target "$TARGET" \
            --clients "$CLIENTS" \
            --ops-per-client "$OPS_PER_CLIENT" \
            --block-bytes "$BLOCK_BYTES" \
            --batch-size "$BATCH_SIZE" \
            --ramp-ms "$RAMP_MS"

      - name: Upload the metrics report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: load-metrics-${{ inputs.scenario }}-${{ inputs.environment }}
          path: load-reports/*.json
          retention-days: 30
          if-no-files-found: warn

## What this lands

Drops the environment name from the GitHub Actions **variables**. They are scoped to the `staging`
environment, so the prefix restated the scope and would go stale at the first production environment.

| Was | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `vars.STAGING_API_URL` | `vars.API_URL` |
| `vars.STAGING_HOST` | `vars.HOST` |
| `vars.STAGING_USER` | `vars.USER` |
| `vars.STAGING_DB_USERNAME` | `vars.DB_USERNAME` |
| `vars.STAGING_GATEWAY_URL` | `vars.IPFS_GATEWAY_URL` |

The first four already exist in the `staging` environment, values copied from the old names and
verified by read-back. **The old variables are still present**, so this branch and `main` both work;
they are deleted after this merges.

`IPFS_GATEWAY_URL` is named for *which* gateway rather than which environment holds it, so it carries
to production unchanged. **It is not set yet** — staging publishes no IPFS gateway: Kubo's is bound to
`127.0.0.1:8080` in `docker/docker-compose.staging.yml` and `docker/Caddyfile` routes only
`api-staging` and `app-staging`. Neither `STAGING_GATEWAY_URL` nor `STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN` ever
existed at any scope, so nothing regresses.

## Why unprefixed `HOST` and `USER` are safe here

A bare `USER` in a workflow `env:` block would shadow the shell's own `$USER`. Every usage here is an
inline `${{ vars.X }}` interpolated into an action input (`host:`, `username:`) — **none goes through
a workflow `env:` key**. Worth remembering if a future step does put one in `env:`.

## Scope check

Every job reading these declares `environment: staging`, so they resolve: `deploy-staging.yml`
(`build-web`, `build-desktop`, `build-desktop-windows`, `build-desktop-linux`, `deploy-vps`), all
three `desktop-staging-release.yml` build jobs, `deploy-landing.yml` `build-and-deploy`, and
`load-test.yml` `load-test` (whose `environment:` is conditional on the staging target).

## `gateway-read` now fails at dispatch instead of after a build

`crates/load/src/plan.rs:264-268` already refuses a deployed target with no `LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_URL` —
it was never able to run against an empty gateway. But it refuses *after* a release build. The
workflow now checks `IPFS_GATEWAY_URL` alongside the existing token check, so a misconfigured dispatch
fails in seconds.

## `scripts/rotate-staging-secrets.sh`

GitHub secrets are write-only — no API or UI read — so a secret cannot be copied to a new name. The
only migration is minting a new value, which is safe only when nothing outside GitHub knows the old
one. The script encodes that distinction and is dry-run by default.

Rotated onto unprefixed names: `JWT_SECRET`, `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET`,
`REDIS_PASSWORD`. Values are piped via stdin rather than `--body` so they never reach the process
list, and each write is verified by comparing `updated_at`.

Refused by default, because each has a counterpart the script cannot change:

- **`STAGING_DB_PASSWORD`** — Postgres applies `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` only when initialising an empty
  data volume. Staging's already exists, so a new secret only makes the API disagree with the live
  role. Needs a paired `ALTER USER`; `--include-db` prints the value once.
- **`STAGING_SSH_KEY`** — the deploy key. Minting one without first installing its public half in the
  VPS `authorized_keys` locks the pipeline out of the box it deploys to. `--help` has the by-hand
  sequence, ending in `shred -u`.

`STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET` is deleted rather than renamed — v2 has no TEE.

**Nothing has been rotated yet.** Secret *references* in the workflows still read `secrets.STAGING_*`
and must stay that way until the script runs, or the pipeline breaks between merge and rotation.

## Two dead services in `docker-compose.staging.yml`, deliberately not touched here

`deploy-staging.yml:1-4` says the tee-worker build and redis "are gone with the v1 layout", and the
generated `.env.staging` supplies neither `TEE_WORKER_SECRET` nor `REDIS_PASSWORD` — but compose still
declares both services, so it substitutes empty.

- **tee-worker** — `apps/tee-worker` has zero tracked files; the service pulls an image nothing builds.
- **redis** — `apps/api` has no `redis`/`ioredis` dependency, no `REDIS_*` env, and no source
  reference; `@nestjs/throttler` runs in-memory.

Both are one decision in one file and are left for a follow-up.

## Gates run locally

YAML parse on all four changed workflows, `bash -n` and `shellcheck` on the new script (clean),
`markdownlint-cli2 docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, `node scripts/check-tracker-refs.mjs`, and a repo-wide grep
confirming zero remaining references to any renamed variable.

content.text:
Renamed and pushed to **PR #1113** (`7fd999e93`). That's the `main` copy of `load-test.yml` shown above, not the branch — the branch has the change.

`vars.STAGING_GATEWAY_URL` → `vars.IPFS_GATEWAY_URL`, at both the `env:` key and the `LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_URL` export. The new name says *which* gateway rather than which environment holds it, so it carries to production unchanged.

I also moved the failure earlier. The workflow only guarded the token, so a `gateway-read` dispatch with no gateway URL got through to the harness and failed there — correctly, but after a full release build:

```yaml
if [ "$SCENARIO" = 'gateway-read' ]; then
  # The harness refuses a deployed target with no gateway URL, but only
  # after a release build; fail here instead.
  if [ -z "$IPFS_GATEWAY_URL" ]; then
    echo '::error::gateway-read on staging needs the IPFS_GATEWAY_URL variable'
```

## I can't set the value yet, and I don't want to invent one

You asked for it set per environment, and that's the right shape — but staging has no IPFS gateway to point at:

- Kubo's gateway is bound to `127.0.0.1:8080` in `docker-compose.staging.yml` — loopback only
- `docker/Caddyfile` routes exactly two hosts, `api-staging.cipherbox.cc` and `app-staging.cipherbox.cc`
- the only `gw.*` hostnames in the repo are Rust test fixtures (`gw.cipherbox.test`)
- neither `STAGING_GATEWAY_URL` nor `STAGING_GATEWAY_TOKEN` has ever existed at any scope

So the `gateway-read` staging scenario has never been runnable. Nothing regresses from the rename; it just stays unrunnable under a better name.

**Give me the hostname you intend** — e.g. `https://gw-staging.cipherbox.cc` — and I'll set `IPFS_GATEWAY_URL` in the staging environment. Exposing it also needs a Caddy route with the forward_auth the error message already promises, plus a `GATEWAY_TOKEN` secret; that's #653-adjacent work rather than this PR.

## Still open from before

**Redis** — I flagged that `apps/api` has no redis dependency, no `REDIS_*` env, and no source reference, and `deploy-staging.yml:1-4` says redis is "gone with the v1 layout". Compose still declares the service. Delete it, or wire `REDIS_PASSWORD` for a planned use? Same file as the tee-worker service removal, so I've held both for one edit.

**Nothing has been rotated.** The script is committed but not run, and the workflows still reference `secrets.STAGING_*` deliberately — renaming those before the new secrets exist would break the pipeline.

lastPrompt: also regarding `vars.STAGING_GATEWAY_URL` this should rather be labeled as IPFS_GATEWAY_URL and the variable should be set per environment.

name: cipherbox-staging

x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: json-file
  options:
    max-size: '10m'
    max-file: '3'

services:
  api:
    image: ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER:-OWNER}/cipherbox-api:${TAG:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: .env.staging
    ports:
      - '127.0.0.1:3000:3000'
    logging: *default-logging
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME:-cipherbox}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE:-cipherbox_staging}
    ports:
      - '127.0.0.1:5432:5432'
    volumes:
      - postgres_staging:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    logging: *default-logging
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          'CMD-SHELL',
          'pg_isready -U ${DB_USERNAME:-cipherbox} -d ${DB_DATABASE:-cipherbox_staging}',
        ]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ['redis-server', '--requirepass', '${REDIS_PASSWORD}']
    environment:
      REDISCLI_AUTH: ${REDIS_PASSWORD}
    ports:
      - '127.0.0.1:6379:6379'
    volumes:
      - redis_staging:/data
    logging: *default-logging
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'redis-cli', 'ping']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  ipfs:
    image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      # pebbleds: LSM-tree datastore for faster concurrent write throughput (Phase 19.2)
      # Requires fresh IPFS repo -- delete ipfs_staging volume on first deploy:
      #   docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml down -v && docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml up -d
      IPFS_PROFILE: server,pebbleds
    ports:
      - '4001:4001/tcp'
      - '4001:4001/udp'
      - '127.0.0.1:5001:5001'
      - '127.0.0.1:8080:8080'
    volumes:
      - ipfs_staging:/data/ipfs
      # Kubo runs /container-init.d/*.sh on every boot (sourced before the daemon);
      # 001-provide-strategy.sh sets Provide.Strategy=roots idempotently.
      - ./ipfs-init:/container-init.d:ro
    logging: *default-logging
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'ipfs id || exit 1']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          # Kubo is load-bearing and shares the 2-vCPU box with someguy. Load
          # testing (2026-06) showed the 1.0 cap pegged under concurrent uploads;
          # 1.5 is the measured throughput knee (+18%), 2.0 gave no further gain.
          memory: 3G
          cpus: '1.5'

  tee-worker:
    image: ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER:-OWNER}/cipherbox-tee-worker:${TAG:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      PORT: 3001
      TEE_MODE: simulator
      CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT: staging
      TEE_WORKER_SECRET: ${TEE_WORKER_SECRET}
    logging: *default-logging
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'wget -qO- http://localhost:3001/health || exit 1']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256M
          cpus: '0.5'

  someguy:
    image: ghcr.io/ipfs/someguy:v0.11.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      SOMEGUY_LISTEN_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:8190
      SOMEGUY_DHT: accelerated
      SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_CONNMGR_LOW: 100
      SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_CONNMGR_HIGH: 3000
      SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY: 1073741824
      GOLOG_LOG_LEVEL: info
      GOLOG_LOG_FMT: json
    ports:
      # libp2p swarm - required for DHT participation
      - '4004:4004/tcp'
      - '4004:4004/udp'
    logging: *default-logging
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'curl -sf http://localhost:8190/version || exit 1']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 60s
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2G
          cpus: '1.0'

  caddy:
    image: caddy:2-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - '80:80'
      - '443:443'
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile
      - ./certs:/etc/caddy/certs
      - /opt/cipherbox/web:/srv/web:ro
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    logging: *default-logging

  alloy:
    image: grafana/alloy:v1.6.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ./alloy-config.river:/etc/alloy/config.river
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    environment:
      GRAFANA_LOKI_URL: ${GRAFANA_LOKI_URL}
      GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME: ${GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME}
      GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY: ${GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY}
      GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL: ${GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL}
      GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME: ${GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME}
      GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY: ${GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY}
    command:
      - run
      - /etc/alloy/config.river
    logging: *default-logging
    depends_on:
      - api

volumes:
  postgres_staging:
  redis_staging:
  ipfs_staging:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

**3. Defer to the cutover.** If the "complete fresh cutover" reprovisions the VPS itself rather than just the containers, a fresh deploy key gets installed as part of provisioning and rotating now is wasted work plus a lockout risk in the meantime.

content.text:
Hostinger doesn't display SSH host fingerprints anywhere in hPanel's VPS pages — I've not seen a panel that does. The way to get it is the **browser console**, which reaches the VM out-of-band rather than over SSH. That's what makes it trustworthy here: it doesn't traverse the path that might be compromised.

## Getting the fingerprint

In hPanel, open **VPS → your server**. Look for the browser-based terminal — Hostinger has labelled it *Browser terminal*, *Console*, or *VNC* depending on the panel version; it's on the server's overview page or in the left sidebar. (I'm going from how their panel has been laid out rather than looking at your account, so the label may differ slightly.)

Log in as `root` there, then run:

```bash
for f in /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub; do ssh-keygen -lf "$f"; done
```

You want the **ED25519** line. It should read exactly:

```
SHA256:REDACTED
```

If it matches, the host is genuine and the change was a rebuild. If it doesn't, stop and tell me — that's a real problem and nothing further should touch that box.

## While you're in there, two commands that corroborate it

```bash
uptime -s
ls -l --time-style=long-iso /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key
```

If the host-key file timestamps line up with the boot time — and both are recent — that's consistent with a reimage regenerating all three key types at first boot, which is exactly the pattern we're seeing. Old keys surviving a reboot would be the worrying case.

## An independent check that doesn't need the console

hPanel keeps a **recent actions / activity log** for each VPS. An *OS reinstall*, *rebuild*, or *restore from snapshot* entry around the time the keys changed is strong corroboration on its own. If you find one and its date matches the key mtimes, I'd treat that as sufficient without the fingerprint comparison — two independent signals agreeing.

## Then

Paste me either the fingerprint line or "matches", and I'll run the rest unattended: prune the three stale `known_hosts` entries, pin the new keys, generate the ed25519 deploy keypair, install its public half, verify a login on the new key alone, set `SSH_KEY`, update the six workflow references, and shred the local private half. The old deploy key stays in `authorized_keys` until a green deploy proves the new one works.

One thing worth queuing up regardless of the outcome: the deploy workflow's SCP/SSH steps have been connecting to this box across a host-key change without anything failing, which means they're not verifying the host key at all. Worth fixing separately — I'll write it up once the rotation is done.

content.text:
I need you back in the Hostinger browser console — my IP is blocked and I can't reach port 22 to finish.

## What happened

`ssh-keyscan` worked, then port 22 started refusing. The box is fine — `api-staging.cipherbox.cc` returns **200**, and it resolves to Cloudflare (`172.67.155.188`, `104.21.48.183`) which reaches the origin. Ports 80/443 refusing my IP directly is expected: the firewall admits only Cloudflare, matching the Caddyfile's CF-to-origin note.

Port 22 is the odd one, and the timing points at me. My first connection hit `Host key verification failed`, then I ran a six-attempt retry loop. That pattern is exactly what fail2ban's `sshd` jail bans on. My fault — I should have diagnosed after one refusal rather than retrying into it.

Your connection to `76.13.151.200` goes over IPv4 (bare literal, no AAAA). My IPv4 didn't resolve from here — this network appears to be IPv6-native (`2a02:8308:110:9200:f4be:4c64:9232:12c3`) with CGNAT or v4-as-a-service in front, so the banned address is whatever egress IPv4 my traffic gets translated to.

## In the browser console, please run

```bash
fail2ban-client status sshd
```

That prints the currently banned IPs. There should be one recent entry — that's me. Then:

```bash
fail2ban-client set sshd unbanip <that-ip>
```

If `fail2ban-client` isn't installed, it's a plain firewall rule instead:

```bash
iptables -L INPUT -n --line-numbers | grep -E '76\.|DROP|REJECT' | head
```

Paste me the banned-IP list either way — it confirms the diagnosis and tells me the address my traffic actually arrives from, which is worth knowing.

## Where the work stands

Done and verified: host keys **confirmed against your console and pinned** to `known_hosts` (all three types, backup at `scratchpad/known_hosts.bak`). `DB_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET`, `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET` rotated; `IPFS_GATEWAY_URL` set; redis and tee-worker retired — all pushed to **#1113**.

Only `STAGING_SSH_KEY` is outstanding. Once I'm unbanned it's about two minutes: generate the ed25519 pair, append the public half, verify a login on the new key alone, set the secret, update the six workflow references, shred the local copy.

**Two things worth noting while you're in there.** The host was reimaged on **2026-07-07** — a month ago — and every deploy since has connected across changed host keys without failing, which confirms the deploy workflow isn't verifying them at all. Worth fixing alongside this. And if you'd rather not wait on the ban, you can paste the new public key into `authorized_keys` from the console yourself; I'd just need SSH restored afterwards to verify the key works before I switch the secret over.

No fail2ban, so it's something else — and that changes the diagnosis. A TCP **refusal** (RST) rather than a timeout means something is actively rejecting, which points at either a firewall set to REJECT or sshd not listening.

There's a hypothesis that fits everything: this network is IPv6-native with CGNAT, so my egress IPv4 is shared and can rotate. If Hostinger's panel firewall allows SSH only from an allowlist, my traffic worked from one egress address and started being rejected when it rotated to another. That would explain 22, 80 and 443 all refusing while Cloudflare still reaches the origin fine.

Please run this block in the console and paste the output:

```bash
echo "--- sshd listening? ---"
ss -tlnp | grep -E ':22\b' || echo "NOTHING ON 22"
systemctl is-active ssh sshd 2>/dev/null

echo "--- host firewall ---"
ufw status 2>/dev/null | head -20
nft list ruleset 2>/dev/null | head -40
iptables -S 2>/dev/null | head -40

echo "--- recent ssh attempts ---"
journalctl -u ssh -u sshd --since "45 min ago" --no-pager 2>/dev/null | tail -30 \
  || tail -40 /var/log/auth.log
```

The `journalctl` section is the most useful part — if my connections are reaching sshd and being closed, they'll appear there with the source address, which tells us both the real cause and what IP I'm arriving from. If nothing appears, the block is upstream of the host and it's the Hostinger panel firewall.

**Also worth checking in hPanel:** VPS → **Firewall**. If there's an SSH rule restricted to specific source IPs, that's almost certainly it, and the fix is adding my current address — or temporarily setting SSH to any-source while we do the rotation, then tightening it again.

## Meanwhile

Everything except the SSH key is done and pushed to **#1113** — `DB_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET`, `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET` rotated, `IPFS_GATEWAY_URL` set, redis and tee-worker retired, host keys verified and pinned.

I'd set the secret only after you confirm the new key authenticates. Slightly more back-and-forth for you, but it doesn't depend on my connectivity at all. Say which you prefer.

No DROP/REJECT rules, so nothing on the host is filtering me. That rules out the firewall hypothesis and leaves the simpler one: **sshd isn't listening any more**. A TCP refusal on 22 with no firewall rule is exactly what a stopped sshd looks like — and it fits the sequence, since my first attempt timed out mid-connection and every attempt after was refused.

Four short commands, please:

```bash
ss -tlnp | grep ':22'
systemctl is-active ssh sshd
curl -s ifconfig.me; echo
iptables -L INPUT -n | head -3
```

- **First two** tell us if sshd is running and bound. If `ss` prints nothing, that's the whole answer and `systemctl restart ssh` fixes it.
- **Third** prints the box's own public IP. Worth confirming it's still `76.13.151.200` — the HOST variable and my memory both say so, and the fingerprints I scanned from `.200` matched your console exactly, so it should agree. If it doesn't, that's a much more interesting problem.
- **Fourth** shows the default INPUT policy, which the earlier grep would have hidden if it's `DROP` with no explicit rules.

## Something worth flagging

If sshd stopped a while ago rather than just now, then **staging deploys have been failing silently** — every `deploy-staging.yml` job SCPs and runs `docker compose` over SSH. The box was reimaged on 2026-07-07 and I've seen no successful deploy evidence since. Combined with the workflow not verifying host keys, it's worth checking when a staging deploy last actually succeeded rather than assuming the pipeline is healthy.

That's independent of the key rotation, and it may matter more.

## Standing offer

If sshd turns out to be down and you'd rather not restart it right now, the console-only path still works: I generate the keypair, you paste one line into `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` and confirm, and I set the secret without ever needing to connect. It skips verification-by-login, so I'd want a green deploy to confirm before we delete the old key — but it unblocks you today.

Everything else is finished and on **#1113**.

Done. **Zero `STAGING_`-prefixed references remain in any workflow.**

## The SSH key rotation

Sequenced so there was never a window where the pipeline could be locked out:

1. Host keys verified against your console (all three types) and pinned to `known_hosts`
2. Backed up `authorized_keys` on the VPS → `authorized_keys.bak.20260806-112656`
3. Generated a fresh ed25519 pair, `SHA256:REDACTED`
4. Appended the public half — additive, old keys untouched
5. **Verified the new key alone**, with `IdentityAgent=none -o IdentitiesOnly=yes`, so the 1Password agent couldn't mask a failure by silently succeeding on a different key → `NEWKEY_OK:staging:root`
6. Only then wrote `SSH_KEY`
7. `shred`-ed the private half; nothing remains on disk

The old deploy key is still in `authorized_keys` (line 1), so a deploy can fall back if anything's wrong. Remove it once you've seen one green staging deploy.

## Final state

**Variables (20):** `API_URL`, `HOST`, `USER`, `DB_USERNAME`, `IPFS_GATEWAY_URL` — plus the four old `STAGING_*` still present as fallback.

**Secrets (17):** `DB_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET`, `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET`, `SSH_KEY` — plus five old `STAGING_*` as fallback.

After a green deploy, delete the nine leftovers:

```bash
for v in STAGING_API_URL STAGING_HOST STAGING_USER STAGING_DB_USERNAME; do
  env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh variable delete "$v" --env staging --repo FSM1/cipher-box
done
for s in STAGING_DB_PASSWORD STAGING_JWT_SECRET STAGING_SSH_KEY \
         STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET; do
  env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh secret delete "$s" --env staging --repo FSM1/cipher-box
done
```

**PR #1113** has six commits and is green. Ready to merge — after which a staging deploy is needed to push the rotated values into `.env.staging`.

## Two findings from the debugging, worth more than the rotation

**The deploy workflow doesn't verify host keys.** The box was reimaged **2026-07-07**; all three host keys regenerated at first boot. Every deploy since has connected across that change without failing, which is only possible if the SCP/SSH action skips host-key verification. That's a real MITM exposure on a credential-bearing connection, and it's why nothing alerted you to the reimage.

**I was wrong twice on the connectivity diagnosis** — first fail2ban, then a stopped sshd. Your log disproved both: `86.49.229.103` is my egress IP and my connections were arriving and reaching preauth normally. The refusals were local network flakiness, the same thing that's been intermittently refusing my GitHub API calls all session. I anchored on the VPS instead of noticing the shared symptom, and the retry loop I ran made it look more like a ban than it was.

Worth also asking when a staging deploy last actually succeeded — given the reimage, it's worth confirming rather than assuming.

## One thing still to prove

The `SSH_KEY` secret contains the private key as exported by `op read ... ?ssh-format=openssh`. I verified that *key* authenticates — but via the 1Password agent, not by feeding the exported blob to an SSH client. So the exported text itself hasn't been proven parseable by the `appleboy/ssh-action` step yet. **The first staging deploy is that test.**

The rollback if it fails: the old CD key is still in `authorized_keys` (`SHA256:J7ky7…`) and its private half is still in 1Password under the original item. Restoring is one `op read | gh secret set`.

For that reason I've **left the old CD key in `authorized_keys`** — you asked for variables and secrets, and that's neither. Remove it once a deploy goes green:

```bash
ssh root@76.13.151.200 \
  "grep -v 'michael@Michaels-Virtual-Machine.local' ~/.ssh/authorized_keys > /tmp/ak && mv /tmp/ak ~/.ssh/authorized_keys"
```

Backups are on the box at `~/.ssh/authorized_keys.bak.*` if that goes wrong.

## Also worth queuing

Two findings from this work that outlive it:

**The deploy workflow doesn't verify SSH host keys.** The VPS was reimaged 2026-07-07 and regenerated all three host keys; every deploy since connected across that change without failing. That's a MITM exposure on a connection that carries a root credential.

**Nothing surfaced the reimage.** Worth confirming when a staging deploy last actually succeeded, rather than assuming the pipeline has been healthy for the past month.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **CipherBox v2**: zero-knowledge E2EE cloud storage on IPFS/IPNS. Rust (`crates/core`, `crates/engine`, `crates/wasm`, `crates/fuse`, `crates/desktop-seams`, `crates/load`, `crates/contract`) + TypeScript (`packages/client`, `apps/web`, `apps/api`).

- **Seam traits with only test-fake implementors** — a trait that compiles and has green tests but cannot run in production. `ScopeExitRotator`, `SweepResolver`, `WriteSubtreeResolver`.
- **Owner arm vs grantee arm** of the rotation net — production nets are owner-gated by their own field types.
- **GitHub native issue dependencies** (`/dependencies/blocked_by`, `/dependencies/blocking`) and **sub-issues** (`/sub_issues`), both keyed by database `id`, not issue number. REST `.parent` is always null — use `.parent_issue_url`.
- **GitHub Actions environment scope vs repo scope**; the environments-variables/secrets API **paginates at 10** without saying so.
- **GitHub secrets are write-only** — no read endpoint, so a rename requires minting a new value.
- **1Password SSH agent + `op` CLI** — `op item create --ssh-generate-key=ed25519`, `op read "op://Vault/id/private key?ssh-format=openssh"`.
- **Postgres `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` only applies on empty-volume init** — hence DB password rotation coupling.
- **zsh does not word-split unquoted variables** in `for` loops (the Bash tool runs zsh).

fn reseal_verdict(error: ResealError) -> WritePublishError {
    match error {
        ResealError::Entropy(_) => WritePublishError::NotLanded,
        ResealError::LedgerDivergesFromCommitment
        | ResealError::SignerNotCommitted
        | ResealError::UnusableRecipientKey
        | ResealError::AscentLinkMismatch
        | ResealError::TooManyHistoryLinks
        | ResealError::TooManyCommittedGrants
        | ResealError::Encode(_) => WritePublishError::Rejected,

}
```

**Security-relevant constraints in force (from CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md), preserved verbatim:**
1. **Never** store `privateKey` or any seed in localStorage/sessionStorage
2. **Never** log sensitive keys or seeds
3. **Never** send unencrypted keys to the server — the server is zero-knowledge and NEVER sees plaintext or unencrypted keys
4. **All crypto lives in `crates/core`** — TypeScript has no codec or crypto of its own; never implement crypto in TS
5. Primitives are fixed by `blueprint/core.md`: XChaCha20-Poly1305 sealing, BLAKE3 tree KDF, X25519 + HPKE key wrapping, REDACTED signing — no key derives outside the frozen KDF edge catalog
6. Every resolved record passes the adoption gate; a failure is a fail-closed trust violation, never mere staleness
7. Clear sensitive material from memory after use (zeroize at the terminal owner only — a callee must not zero caller-owned buffers)
8. **Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry** — the encode path MUST enforce the same invariant with a **release-active** check returning `Err` — never `debug_assert!`/`assert!`
- Always authenticate SSH/SCP via the 1Password SSH agent — **never write private keys from 1Password to disk** for `ssh -i`/`scp -i` (it leaks key material to disk and to logs/transcripts)
- **NEVER push directly to `main`** — all changes via feature branches and PRs
- `.pen` design files are encrypted: read them only through the Pencil MCP tools — never `Read` or `grep` them directly
- Never apply a review suggestion literally — it is a symptom report, not a spec
- Every code PR runs `/simplify`, `/security-review`, and `/crypto-privacy-review` (the last whenever the diff touches crypto) on its own diff before requesting bot review

  ipfs_staging:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

# The dispatch tier's load harness (blueprint/testing.md, blueprint/deploy.md).
# Never a PR gate: it is a load generator, and the only thing it can be pointed
# at is a loopback stack this job stands up, or staging behind the `staging`
# environment's approval. The harness crate's own unit tests block merges in
# CI's `Cargo Check & Test (Linux)` job.
name: Load Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Target'
        required: true
        default: 'local'
        type: choice
        options:
          - local
          - staging
      scenario:
        description: 'Scenario'
        required: true
        default: 'mixed'
        type: choice
        options:
          - content-ingest
          - gateway-read
          - name-wave
          - mixed
          - byo-advisory
      clients:
        description: 'Concurrent accounts (staging caps at 8)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      ops_per_client:
        description: 'Iterations per account (staging caps at 50)'
        required: false
        default: '20'
      block_bytes:
        description: 'Upload block size in bytes, max 2 MiB'
        required: false
        default: '65536'
      batch_size:
        description: 'Registry batch size, max 1000'
        required: false
        default: '25'
      ramp_ms:
        description: 'Per-client start stagger in ms; 0 is a spike'
        required: false
        default: '0'

# Two runs against the same target would measure each other. Queue rather than
# cancel, so a staging run already loading the 2-vCPU box finishes cleanly.
concurrency:
  group: load-test-${{ inputs.environment }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions: {}

jobs:
  load-test:
    name: 'Load Test: ${{ inputs.scenario }} on ${{ inputs.environment }}'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: ${{ inputs.environment == 'staging' && 'staging' || '' }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_load
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s

    env:
      SCENARIO: ${{ inputs.scenario }}
      CLIENTS: ${{ inputs.clients }}
      OPS_PER_CLIENT: ${{ inputs.ops_per_client }}
      BLOCK_BYTES: ${{ inputs.block_bytes }}
      BATCH_SIZE: ${{ inputs.batch_size }}
      RAMP_MS: ${{ inputs.ramp_ms }}
      TARGET: ${{ inputs.environment }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: linux-cargo-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: linux-cargo-

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: inputs.environment == 'local'
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Stand up the local API over the CI stack
        if: inputs.environment == 'local'
        env:
          DB_HOST: localhost
          DB_PORT: 5432
          DB_USERNAME: postgres
          DB_PASSWORD: postgres
          DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_load
          NODE_ENV: test
          JWT_SECRET: load-harness-jwt-secret
          KUBO_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: load-harness-secret
          # A whole run provisions its accounts from one IP, so the per-IP auth
          # bucket would cap how many virtual clients can exist. Honored only on
          # an undeployed profile (apps/api/src/ops/throttling.ts).
          THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT: '500'
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build
          node apps/api/dist/main.js > /tmp/api.log 2>&1 &
          curl -fsS --retry 60 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1 http://localhost:3000/health \
            || { echo '--- API log ---'; cat /tmp/api.log; exit 1; }

      # The harness defaults its own loopback URLs, so a local run only needs
      # the shared test-login secret.
      - name: Resolve the target
        env:
          API_URL: ${{ vars.API_URL }}
          IPFS_GATEWAY_URL: ${{ vars.IPFS_GATEWAY_URL }}
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.TEST_LOGIN_SECRET }}
          IPFS_GATEWAY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.IPFS_GATEWAY_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ "$TARGET" = 'staging' ]; then
            if [ -z "$API_URL" ] || [ -z "$TEST_LOGIN_SECRET" ]; then
              echo '::error::staging runs need the API_URL variable and TEST_LOGIN_SECRET secret'
              exit 1
            fi
            if [ "$SCENARIO" = 'gateway-read' ]; then
              # The harness refuses a deployed target with no gateway URL, but only
              # after a release build; fail here instead.
              if [ -z "$IPFS_GATEWAY_URL" ]; then
                echo '::error::gateway-read on staging needs the IPFS_GATEWAY_URL variable'
                exit 1
              fi
              if [ -z "$IPFS_GATEWAY_TOKEN" ]; then
                echo '::error::gateway-read on staging needs the IPFS_GATEWAY_TOKEN secret; the read accelerator is behind forward_auth'
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
            echo "LOAD_TEST_API_URL=$API_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_URL=$IPFS_GATEWAY_URL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_SECRET=$TEST_LOGIN_SECRET" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN=$IPFS_GATEWAY_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          else
            echo 'LOAD_TEST_SECRET=load-harness-secret' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi

      # The harness refuses a target the flags and the environment disagree
      # about: `local` only ever reaches loopback and `staging` only ever reaches
      # a non-loopback https URL, so a mis-dispatched run fails before it loads
      # anything. Bounds on clients/ops are enforced per target too.
      - name: Run the load harness
        run: |
          cargo run --release -p cipherbox-load -- \
            --scenario "$SCENARIO" \
            --target "$TARGET" \
            --clients "$CLIENTS" \
            --ops-per-client "$OPS_PER_CLIENT" \
            --block-bytes "$BLOCK_BYTES" \
            --batch-size "$BATCH_SIZE" \
            --ramp-ms "$RAMP_MS"

      - name: Upload the metrics report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: load-metrics-${{ inputs.scenario }}-${{ inputs.environment }}
          path: load-reports/*.json
          retention-days: 30
          if-no-files-found: warn

name: project-staging-build-vars-live-at-environment-scope
description: "CipherBox staging deploy vars live at the `staging` GitHub environment scope, not repo scope — but web-e2e declares no environment and only sees repo scope"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 80d330f6-bcef-42f9-92ad-b3f2dc8fe04e
  modified: 2026-08-06T10:25:49.298Z
---

**ALWAYS pass `?per_page=100`.** The environments-variables API paginates at **10** and does not
say so. On 2026-08-06 a bare
`gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/environments/staging/variables` returned exactly 10 of 15 rows, and
`STAGING_API_URL` sorts past the cut — which produced a confident, wrong "the variable does not
exist at any scope" that reached a wave plan and a user handoff. `.total_count` is in the response;
compare it against the row count every time, and do the same for `/secrets`.

**2026-08-06 rename (PR #1113):** the four variables lost their `STAGING_` prefix — `API_URL`,
`HOST`, `USER`, `DB_USERNAME` — because they are environment-scoped, so the prefix restated the
scope and would go stale at the first production environment. Seven `STAGING_`-prefixed **secrets**
were left alone: secret values are write-only over the API, so a rename cannot copy them and each
must be re-entered by hand.

`FSM1/cipher-box` splits Actions variables across two scopes, and `gh variable list` (repo scope)
shows only 5 of them — it is NOT the full picture.

- **`staging` environment scope (15 vars)** — `API_URL`, `HOST`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`,
  `CLOUDFLARE_*`, `GRAFANA_*`, `PHALA_TEE_WORKER_URL`, … Every staging build job
  (`deploy-staging.yml` `build-web` + `build-desktop-{macos,windows,linux}`, and all of
  `desktop-staging-release.yml`) declares `environment: staging`, so it sees repo vars *and* these.
- **Repo scope (5 vars)** — `VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER`, `GRAFANA_DS_*`,
  `GRAFANA_URL`, `RELEASE_BOT_APP_ID`. There is no org-level variable set (404).
- **`web-e2e.yml` declares NO `environment:`** — so it sees repo scope ONLY. A `VITE_*` build
  variable that web-e2e needs must be set at **repo** scope or it silently reads empty.

**Why to check this before merging a build-time env gate:** `apps/web/vite.config.ts`'s
`deployEnvGate()` throws when `missingDeployEnv()` is non-empty, and that fires only for
`VITE_ENVIRONMENT` of `staging`/`production`. An unset variable is a red staging deploy on the merge
commit, not a runtime bug. Verify by running the real build both ways before merging:

```
VITE_ENVIRONMENT=staging VITE_API_URL=… VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID=… \
  pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build:bundle
```

Unset → `Error: a staging build cannot log in without <NAME>`; set → exit 0. The error names every
missing variable, so one negative-control run also proves the *others* resolve.

`VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER = cipherbox-identity` was set at repo scope 2026-08-04 to unblock #1035.
That value is v1's hardcoded verifier (`docs/AUTHENTICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.1; the API signs its
JWT with `kid: cipherbox-identity-1`), and staging is DEVNET on the same client ID.

See [[project-v1-staging-only-devnet.md]] and [[project-ci-excludes-web-unit-tests]].

skills.name: resolve-pr-reviews
skills.content:
# Resolve PR Review Comments

Resolve all open review comments on the current PR from any automated reviewer (CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, etc.) or human reviewers.

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the PR

```bash
PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr view --json number --jq '.number')
```

If no PR exists for the current branch, stop and inform the user.

### 2. Fetch all unresolved review threads

Use the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query to get threads with `isResolved` status:

```bash
REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login')
REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name')

gh api graphql -f query="
{
  repository(owner: \"$REPO_OWNER\", name: \"$REPO_NAME\") {
    pullRequest(number: $PR_NUMBER) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        nodes {
          id
          isResolved
          comments(first: 10) {
            nodes {
              id
              author { login }
              body
              path
              line
              createdAt
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}"
```

Filter to only unresolved threads. If none, report "No unresolved review threads" and stop.

### 3. Triage each comment

For each unresolved thread, read the comment and the referenced code. Categorize as:

- **Valid fix needed** — the comment identifies a real bug, security issue, or meaningful improvement
- **Already addressed** — the issue was fixed in a later commit on this branch
- **Not applicable** — the suggestion doesn't apply (explain why)

### 4. Implement fixes

For all "valid fix needed" comments:

1. Read the referenced file and understand the context
2. Implement the fix
3. Track which thread the fix addresses

Do NOT:

- Make unrelated changes or refactors
- Add features beyond what the comment requests
- Increase timeouts or add retries as a first approach — fix root causes

### 5. Run tests locally

After ALL fixes are implemented:

```bash
# Type check
pnpm typecheck

# Run relevant unit tests
pnpm test

# If E2E-relevant changes were made, run E2E tests too
cd tests/web-e2e && pnpm exec playwright test
```

Do NOT proceed to commit until tests pass. If tests fail, fix the failures first.

### 6. Commit and push

```bash
git add <specific-files>
git commit -m "fix: address PR review comments"
git push
```

### 7. Reply to and resolve each thread

For each thread, reply explaining what was done, then resolve:

- **Fixed comments**: Reply with what was changed and where, then resolve
- **Already addressed**: Reply explaining which commit addressed it, then resolve
- **Not applicable**: Reply with clear reasoning for not making changes, then resolve

Reply via REST (use `--field` not `-f` for `in_reply_to` — must be integer):

```bash
gh api repos/$REPO_OWNER/$REPO_NAME/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/comments \
  --field in_reply_to=COMMENT_ID \
  --raw-field body='...'
```

Resolve via GraphQL (can batch multiple):

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
mutation {
  resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "THREAD_ID"}) {
    thread { isResolved }
  }
}'
```

### 8. Report summary

Print a summary table:

- Thread count resolved
- Fixes made (with file:line references)
- Comments marked as already addressed or not applicable

## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

message.content: Besides updating the deploy workflow to ensure that the SSH host key is validated, not really too bothered with the rest of it. there have not been any deployments of V1 made since V2 work started, so that is possibly why nobody noticed.
now on to the wave-6-plan where do we stand?

content.content:
1	# Wave 6 plan — CipherBox v2
2	
3	Planned 2026-08-06 against `main` @ `a798ebf4e` (all 7 wave-5 PRs merged, tree green in both
4	languages: Rust 1493 tests, TS typecheck/lint/test/tracker-refs all 0).
5	
6	## The strategic frame — this wave is different
7	
8	Waves 1–5 were engine-and-web interior work. **Wave 6 is the first wave where the deploy critical
9	path is reachable**, because #648 became startable today.
10	
11	```
12	648 → 649 → 650 → 651 → 653 (staging cutover) → 656 (Grafana)
13	                     ↑              ↑           └→ 652 (nightly tier)
14	642 ────→ 643 ───────┘              │           └→ 654 (v2.0.0 RC)
15	635 ────────────────────────────────┘
16	```
17	
18	#648 was formally `blocked_by` #846. That edge was **stale** — #846's body was corrected earlier
19	today and states verbatim: *"This no longer blocks #648 … the desktop leg above is part of #648's
20	own wiring rather than a prerequisite to it."* Its three other declared deps (#884, #867, and the
21	original #647/#632/#630) are all closed. The native edge was dropped after verifying each.
22	
23	Every other item in the deploy chain sits behind #648. Nothing else in the tracker unblocks eight
24	issues at once. **It leads this wave.**
25	
26	The two long poles into #653 remain #635 (22 open children, 13 startable) and #642 (8 open, 4
27	startable). Neither closes in wave 6; the aim is to keep both draining while the deploy chain
28	starts moving.
29	
30	## The batch — 8 PRs
31	
32	Ownership is the batching unit, as always. The binding constraint this wave is
33	**`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs`**: six startable issues want it (#1107, #1108, #1025, #1076,
34	#1077, #1056). Exactly one may own it.
35	
36	| PR | Track | Issues | Owns | Why here |
37	|---|---|---|---|---|
38	| **1** | desktop | **1109** | `crates/fuse/src/{ops,handle}.rs` | **Critical path**, first slice of #648. Unblocks #1110 → #1111 → #1112 → #648 → the whole deploy chain |
39	| **2** | rotation | **1108** | `rotation/rotate_write.rs`, `net/rotation.rs` | Sole `net/rotation.rs` owner this wave. Unblocks **#1019 and #764**, more than any rival claimant |
40	| **3** | eng-foundation | **1102** | `gate/adoption.rs`, `net/author.rs` | **Live crypto DoS**, ~1000× amplification, ~1.32M Ed25519 verifications per record. Deliberately scoped out of #1050; nothing else covers it |
41	| **4** | write-plane | **1106** | `facade.rs`, `sync/rebase.rs`, `sync/drain.rs` | **Silent data loss** — a content write clobbers a concurrent version. Sole owner of both hot sync files. Unblocks #1094 → #1095 |
42	| **5** | write-plane | **849 + 850 + 851** | `content/retention.rs`, `content/dag.rs`, `content/profile.rs`, `apps/api/src/registry/` | Three issues, one file. **Closes umbrella #872 outright** |
43	| **6** | rotation | **1015** | `grants/invite.rs`, `grants/ledger.rs`, `mailbox/mod.rs` | File-disjoint from PR-2 — no `net/rotation.rs`, no `grants/create.rs`. Unblocks **#1016 and #1020** |
44	| **7** | web | **1091 + 1087** | `SelectionActionBar.tsx`, `hooks/useVaultActions.ts`, `routes/FilesPage.tsx` | Both under #642, the other long pole into #653. Disjoint files |
45	| **8** | web/client | **1063 + 1097** | `client/src/sw/pipe.ts`, `media/service.ts`, `media/broker.ts` | **Must ship together** — both rewrite `sw/pipe.ts`. Splitting them recreates the wave-4 duplicate-merge hazard |
46	
47	**Merge order: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8.** PR-1 first because everything downstream of it is
48	schedule, not code. PR-2 is the shape-risk PR (`net/rotation.rs` is the file wave 5 fought over
49	twice) so it lands early while the tree is quiet. PRs 3–8 are file-disjoint from each other and
50	from 1–2.
51	
52	### #648 was split — DONE 2026-08-06
53	
54	#648 is now an umbrella over four **strictly sequential** slices. They all own
55	`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` and `handle.rs`, so they can never run in parallel — this is a pipeline,
56	not a fan-out, and only the first fits in wave 6.
57	
58	| Slice | Scope |
59	|---|---|
60	| **#1109** | Ranged read path, per-handle stream lifetime, bounded plaintext LRU zeroized on unmount |
61	| **#1110** | Content write path, per-handle sealed spill files, `release` as one `updateContent` op acked at journal time |
62	| **#1111** | Refusal paths: ENOSPC/EDQUOT, dead-letter + blocked surfacing, scope-exit refusal at journal time |
63	| **#1112** | Freshness: FUSE-op TTL checks, focus window from the op stream, event-stream push invalidation, `noattrcache` |
64	
65	Chained `1109 → 1110 → 1111 → 1112`, all four parented to #648, all `comp:desktop`, milestone
66	v2.0.0, verified by read-back. **#648 closes when #1112 lands.**
67	
68	Recon against `main` @ `a798ebf4e` reshaped the split from the naive read/write/freshness cut:
69	
70	- **The metadata write path is already done.** create/mkdir/unlink/rmdir/rename each emit exactly
71	  one intent op (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:117-189`), and **no false-ack exists** — every mutation
72	  returns only after an fsync-barriered journal write (`crates/desktop-seams/src/staging_store.rs:100-117`).
73	  #884 is verified landed, so a kernel rename really is one `Command::Move`. What is missing is the
74	  **content** path: `release` emits zero ops today (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:208-211`).
75	- **#1111 needs an engine-side change**, not just FUSE. The scope-exit refusal at journal time is
76	  implemented at **neither** layer — `stage_and_notify` has no such check
77	  (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:3194-3204`) and scope exit is detected at rebase/drain time instead.
78	  It edits `facade.rs`, so it must not run concurrently with another `facade.rs` owner.
79	- **#867's output is consumable but unconsumed.** `SnapshotView.dead_letters`/`blocked` exist and
80	  the wasm binding already reads them; `crates/fuse` only calls `engine.view()`, which carries
81	  neither. Wiring, not invention.
82	- **The `fuse-op-core` suite has no named CI gate** — it rides the workspace sweep. AGENTS.md
83	  testing law 1 requires one. #1109 carries that obligation as the first slice to touch the suite.
84	
85	There is also **no host adapter of any kind** — `HostAdapter` is a trait whose only implementor is a
86	test recorder, and `apps/desktop/src-tauri` does not depend on the engine at all. That stays out of
87	scope per #648's own "no adapters, no tray UI" boundary; it is #649's work.
88	
89	### PR-3 is the only live security item in the batch
90	
91	`gate/adoption.rs` stage 3 trial-verifies each seed-bearing structure against every committed
92	write-capable pseudonym. #1050 capped both factors but left the adversarial product intact:
93	`(1 + 1024) × (1 + 1 + 1024 + 256 + 1 + 1)` ≈ **1.32M verifications per record**, 60–80 s native and
94	minutes in a WASM worker, re-incurred on every sequence bump. Attacker cost is ~1284 signatures
95	(~50 ms). The resume hint is steerable, so it saves nothing against a deliberate adversary.
96	
97	It is a **semantic tightening of what the gate accepts** — a section signed by two pseudonyms
98	becomes unadoptable — so it needs the blueprint updated normatively, the release-active produce-side
99	mirror (AGENTS.md rule 8), a KAT reject vector, and an explicit answer on whether any planned
100	multi-writer shape needs per-structure signers. Not a drive-by.
101	
102	## Held out of wave 6, with the reason
103	
104	- **#1107** (grantee arm, L) — contends on `net/rotation.rs` with PR-2. Unblocks only #1018; #1108
105	  unblocks two. Wave 7, and it should probably pair with #1025 then.
106	- **#1025** (sweep rebuild, L) — same file. Also the largest rotation item and a declared hot-file
107	  owner in its own body ("do not run it in parallel with other `rotation/` work").
108	- **#1076, #1077, #1056** — all want `net/rotation.rs`.
