# Wave 6 plan — CipherBox v2

Planned 2026-08-06 against `main` @ `a798ebf4e` (all 7 wave-5 PRs merged, tree green in both
languages: Rust 1493 tests, TS typecheck/lint/test/tracker-refs all 0).

## The strategic frame — this wave is different

Waves 1–5 were engine-and-web interior work. **Wave 6 is the first wave where the deploy critical
path is reachable**, because #648 became startable today.

```
648 → 649 → 650 → 651 → 653 (staging cutover) → 656 (Grafana)
                     ↑              ↑           └→ 652 (nightly tier)
642 ────→ 643 ───────┘              │           └→ 654 (v2.0.0 RC)
635 ────────────────────────────────┘
```

#648 was formally `blocked_by` #846. That edge was **stale** — #846's body was corrected earlier
today and states verbatim: *"This no longer blocks #648 … the desktop leg above is part of #648's
own wiring rather than a prerequisite to it."* Its three other declared deps (#884, #867, and the
original #647/#632/#630) are all closed. The native edge was dropped after verifying each.

Every other item in the deploy chain sits behind #648. Nothing else in the tracker unblocks eight
issues at once. **It leads this wave.**

The two long poles into #653 remain #635 (22 open children, 13 startable) and #642 (8 open, 4
startable). Neither closes in wave 6; the aim is to keep both draining while the deploy chain
starts moving.

## The batch — 8 PRs

Ownership is the batching unit, as always. The binding constraint this wave is
**`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs`**: six startable issues want it (#1107, #1108, #1025, #1076,
#1077, #1056). Exactly one may own it.

| PR | Track | Issues | Owns | Why here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | desktop | **1109** | `crates/fuse/src/{ops,handle}.rs` | **Critical path**, first slice of #648. Unblocks #1110 → #1111 → #1112 → #648 → the whole deploy chain |
| **2** | rotation | **1108** | `rotation/rotate_write.rs`, `net/rotation.rs` | Sole `net/rotation.rs` owner this wave. Unblocks **#1019 and #764**, more than any rival claimant |
| **3** | eng-foundation | **1102** | `gate/adoption.rs`, `net/author.rs` | **Live crypto DoS**, ~1000× amplification, ~1.32M Ed25519 verifications per record. Deliberately scoped out of #1050; nothing else covers it |
| **4** | write-plane | **1106** | `facade.rs`, `sync/rebase.rs`, `sync/drain.rs` | **Silent data loss** — a content write clobbers a concurrent version. Sole owner of both hot sync files. Unblocks #1094 → #1095 |
| **5** | write-plane | **849 + 850 + 851** | `content/retention.rs`, `content/dag.rs`, `content/profile.rs`, `apps/api/src/registry/` | Three issues, one file. **Closes umbrella #872 outright** |
| **6** | rotation | **1015** | `grants/invite.rs`, `grants/ledger.rs`, `mailbox/mod.rs` | File-disjoint from PR-2 — no `net/rotation.rs`, no `grants/create.rs`. Unblocks **#1016 and #1020** |
| **7** | web | **1091 + 1087** | `SelectionActionBar.tsx`, `hooks/useVaultActions.ts`, `routes/FilesPage.tsx` | Both under #642, the other long pole into #653. Disjoint files |
| **8** | web/client | **1063 + 1097** | `client/src/sw/pipe.ts`, `media/service.ts`, `media/broker.ts` | **Must ship together** — both rewrite `sw/pipe.ts`. Splitting them recreates the wave-4 duplicate-merge hazard |

**Merge order: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8.** PR-1 first because everything downstream of it is
schedule, not code. PR-2 is the shape-risk PR (`net/rotation.rs` is the file wave 5 fought over
twice) so it lands early while the tree is quiet. PRs 3–8 are file-disjoint from each other and
from 1–2.

### #648 was split — DONE 2026-08-06

#648 is now an umbrella over four **strictly sequential** slices. They all own
`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` and `handle.rs`, so they can never run in parallel — this is a pipeline,
not a fan-out, and only the first fits in wave 6.

| Slice | Scope |
|---|---|
| **#1109** | Ranged read path, per-handle stream lifetime, bounded plaintext LRU zeroized on unmount |
| **#1110** | Content write path, per-handle sealed spill files, `release` as one `updateContent` op acked at journal time |
| **#1111** | Refusal paths: ENOSPC/EDQUOT, dead-letter + blocked surfacing, scope-exit refusal at journal time |
| **#1112** | Freshness: FUSE-op TTL checks, focus window from the op stream, event-stream push invalidation, `noattrcache` |

Chained `1109 → 1110 → 1111 → 1112`, all four parented to #648, all `comp:desktop`, milestone
v2.0.0, verified by read-back. **#648 closes when #1112 lands.**

Recon against `main` @ `a798ebf4e` reshaped the split from the naive read/write/freshness cut:

- **The metadata write path is already done.** create/mkdir/unlink/rmdir/rename each emit exactly
  one intent op (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:117-189`), and **no false-ack exists** — every mutation
  returns only after an fsync-barriered journal write (`crates/desktop-seams/src/staging_store.rs:100-117`).
  #884 is verified landed, so a kernel rename really is one `Command::Move`. What is missing is the
  **content** path: `release` emits zero ops today (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:208-211`).
- **#1111 needs an engine-side change**, not just FUSE. The scope-exit refusal at journal time is
  implemented at **neither** layer — `stage_and_notify` has no such check
  (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:3194-3204`) and scope exit is detected at rebase/drain time instead.
  It edits `facade.rs`, so it must not run concurrently with another `facade.rs` owner.
- **#867's output is consumable but unconsumed.** `SnapshotView.dead_letters`/`blocked` exist and
  the wasm binding already reads them; `crates/fuse` only calls `engine.view()`, which carries
  neither. Wiring, not invention.
- **The `fuse-op-core` suite has no named CI gate** — it rides the workspace sweep. AGENTS.md
  testing law 1 requires one. #1109 carries that obligation as the first slice to touch the suite.

There is also **no host adapter of any kind** — `HostAdapter` is a trait whose only implementor is a
test recorder, and `apps/desktop/src-tauri` does not depend on the engine at all. That stays out of
scope per #648's own "no adapters, no tray UI" boundary; it is #649's work.

### PR-3 is the only live security item in the batch

`gate/adoption.rs` stage 3 trial-verifies each seed-bearing structure against every committed
write-capable pseudonym. #1050 capped both factors but left the adversarial product intact:
`(1 + 1024) × (1 + 1 + 1024 + 256 + 1 + 1)` ≈ **1.32M verifications per record**, 60–80 s native and
minutes in a WASM worker, re-incurred on every sequence bump. Attacker cost is ~1284 signatures
(~50 ms). The resume hint is steerable, so it saves nothing against a deliberate adversary.

It is a **semantic tightening of what the gate accepts** — a section signed by two pseudonyms
becomes unadoptable — so it needs the blueprint updated normatively, the release-active produce-side
mirror (AGENTS.md rule 8), a KAT reject vector, and an explicit answer on whether any planned
multi-writer shape needs per-structure signers. Not a drive-by.

        uses: appleboy/scp-action@ff85246acaad7bdce478db94a363cd2bf7c90345 # v1.0.0
        with:

          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}

        with:

          username: ${{ vars.USER }}

- name: Install and build
        working-directory: landing
        run: |
          pnpm install --ignore-workspace --frozen-lockfile
          pnpm run build

      - name: Upload dist to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@ff85246acaad7bdce478db94a363cd2bf7c90345 # v1.0.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          source: 'landing/dist/*'
          target: /tmp/cipherbox-landing
          strip_components: 2

      - name: Pin to IPFS via Kubo
        id: ipfs
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@0ff4204d59e8e51228ff73bce53f80d53301dee2 # v1.2.5
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          capture_stdout: true
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail
            # Kubo runs as a Docker container on the staging host (compose service
            # "ipfs", image ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0) — there is no host-level ipfs CLI, so a
            # bare `ipfs` here fails with "command not found". Run it inside the container.
            # Capture the container list first, THEN take the first line: piping
            # `docker ps` straight into `head` can SIGPIPE docker ps (exit 141) under
            # `pipefail` and abort before the empty-KUBO guard runs.
            KUBO_IDS=$(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0)
            KUBO=$(printf '%s\n' "${KUBO_IDS}" | head -n1)

deploy-vps:
    name: Deploy to Staging VPS
    needs: [build-api, build-web]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Download web dist artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: web-dist
          path: web-dist/

      - name: Generate .env.staging
        run: |
          cat > .env.staging << 'ENVEOF'
          NODE_ENV=staging
          CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=staging
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=${{ secrets.TEST_LOGIN_SECRET }}
          PORT=3000
          DB_HOST=postgres
          DB_PORT=5432

name: Deploy Landing Page to IPFS

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'landing/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-landing.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  build-and-deploy:
    name: Build & Pin to IPFS
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'
          cache-dependency-path: landing/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Install and build
        working-directory: landing
        run: |
          pnpm install --ignore-workspace --frozen-lockfile
          pnpm run build

      - name: Upload dist to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@ff85246acaad7bdce478db94a363cd2bf7c90345 # v1.0.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          fingerprint: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
          source: 'landing/dist/*'
          target: /tmp/cipherbox-landing
          strip_components: 2

      - name: Pin to IPFS via Kubo
        id: ipfs
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@0ff4204d59e8e51228ff73bce53f80d53301dee2 # v1.2.5
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          fingerprint: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
          capture_stdout: true
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail
            # Kubo runs as a Docker container on the staging host (compose service
            # "ipfs", image ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0) — there is no host-level ipfs CLI, so a
            # bare `ipfs` here fails with "command not found". Run it inside the container.
            # Capture the container list first, THEN take the first line: piping
            # `docker ps` straight into `head` can SIGPIPE docker ps (exit 141) under
            # `pipefail` and abort before the empty-KUBO guard runs.
            KUBO_IDS=$(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0)
            KUBO=$(printf '%s\n' "${KUBO_IDS}" | head -n1)
            if [ -z "${KUBO}" ]; then
              echo "::error::No running ipfs/kubo container found on staging host"
              exit 1
            fi
            # The SCP step landed the build at host /tmp/cipherbox-landing; the container
            # has no /tmp bind-mount, so copy it in before adding. Redirect docker cp's
            # stdout to stderr so capture_stdout returns ONLY the CID.
            docker cp /tmp/cipherbox-landing "${KUBO}:/tmp/cipherbox-landing" 1>&2
            CID=$(docker exec "${KUBO}" ipfs add -Qr --pin /tmp/cipherbox-landing)
            # Emit the CID immediately — the pin is already committed to Kubo, so a failure
            # in the best-effort cleanup below must never drop it from stdout (that would
            # fail the step and leave DNSLink pointing at the now-stale CID).
            echo "${CID}"
            docker exec "${KUBO}" rm -rf /tmp/cipherbox-landing || true
            rm -rf /tmp/cipherbox-landing || true

      - name: Validate CID
        env:
          # appleboy/ssh-action's capture_stdout appends the drone-ssh banner
          # ("✅ Successfully executed commands to all hosts") to the remote stdout,
          # so outputs.stdout is MULTI-LINE even though the script echoes only the CID.
          # Pass it via env (not inline ${{ }} interpolation) to avoid script injection.
          RAW_STDOUT: ${{ steps.ipfs.outputs.stdout }}
        run: |
          # Extract just the IPFS CID (CIDv0 "Qm…" or CIDv1 "baf…") from the captured
          # output. A bare multi-line value breaks `>> "$GITHUB_ENV"` with
          # "Unable to process file command 'env' … Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'name')".
          CID=$(printf '%s\n' "$RAW_STDOUT" | grep -oE -m1 'Qm[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{44}|baf[a-z2-7]{20,}')
          if [ -z "${CID}" ]; then
            echo "::error::No CID returned from IPFS pin step"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "CID=${CID}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "Pinned landing page to IPFS: ${CID}"

      - name: Update DNSLink
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID }}
          DNSLINK_RECORD_ID: ${{ secrets.DNSLINK_RECORD_ID }}
        run: |
          curl -sS -X PUT \
            "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/${CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID}/dns_records/${DNSLINK_RECORD_ID}" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            --data "{\"type\":\"TXT\",\"name\":\"_dnslink.cipherbox.cc\",\"content\":\"dnslink=/ipfs/${CID}\"}"

          echo "Updated DNSLink to /ipfs/${CID}"

      - name: Summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          {
            echo "## Landing Page Deployed"
            echo "- **CID:** ${CID}"
            echo "- **IPFS Gateway:** https://ipfs.io/ipfs/${CID}"
            echo "- **Commit:** ${{ github.sha }}"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

**macroscope credits are exhausted** (since ~00:54Z yesterday). Six of wave 5's seven PRs got one bot verdict instead of two. Wave 6 has two XL items and a crypto tightening — worth topping up first.

**`Web E2E Smoke Result` is a flaky required check** (`smoke.spec.ts:43`, sign-out). It failed an engine-only PR in wave 5 and passed on re-run. Every agent needs to know to re-run before triaging.

Say the word and I'll launch. Given eight concurrent worktree agents, I'd suggest **1–4 first** (the critical path plus both live bugs), then 5–8 once the first set is in review — that keeps the review queue from becoming the bottleneck the way it did in wave 4.

name: Deploy Landing Page to IPFS

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'landing/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-landing.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  build-and-deploy:
    name: Build & Pin to IPFS
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # appleboy's actions skip host-key verification when `fingerprint` is empty,
      # so an unset variable would silently restore the trust-on-first-use hole.
      - name: Require a pinned host key
        env:
          SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT" ]; then
            echo '::error::the staging environment needs the SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT variable (ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 HOST | ssh-keygen -lf -)'
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'
          cache-dependency-path: landing/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Install and build
        working-directory: landing
        run: |
          pnpm install --ignore-workspace --frozen-lockfile
          pnpm run build

      - name: Upload dist to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@ff85246acaad7bdce478db94a363cd2bf7c90345 # v1.0.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          fingerprint: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
          source: 'landing/dist/*'
          target: /tmp/cipherbox-landing
          strip_components: 2

      - name: Pin to IPFS via Kubo
        id: ipfs
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@0ff4204d59e8e51228ff73bce53f80d53301dee2 # v1.2.5
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_KEY }}
          fingerprint: ${{ vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT }}
          capture_stdout: true
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail
            # Kubo runs as a Docker container on the staging host (compose service
            # "ipfs", image ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0) — there is no host-level ipfs CLI, so a
            # bare `ipfs` here fails with "command not found". Run it inside the container.
            # Capture the container list first, THEN take the first line: piping
            # `docker ps` straight into `head` can SIGPIPE docker ps (exit 141) under
            # `pipefail` and abort before the empty-KUBO guard runs.
            KUBO_IDS=$(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0)
            KUBO=$(printf '%s\n' "${KUBO_IDS}" | head -n1)
            if [ -z "${KUBO}" ]; then
              echo "::error::No running ipfs/kubo container found on staging host"
              exit 1
            fi
            # The SCP step landed the build at host /tmp/cipherbox-landing; the container
            # has no /tmp bind-mount, so copy it in before adding. Redirect docker cp's
            # stdout to stderr so capture_stdout returns ONLY the CID.
            docker cp /tmp/cipherbox-landing "${KUBO}:/tmp/cipherbox-landing" 1>&2
            CID=$(docker exec "${KUBO}" ipfs add -Qr --pin /tmp/cipherbox-landing)
            # Emit the CID immediately — the pin is already committed to Kubo, so a failure
            # in the best-effort cleanup below must never drop it from stdout (that would
            # fail the step and leave DNSLink pointing at the now-stale CID).
            echo "${CID}"
            docker exec "${KUBO}" rm -rf /tmp/cipherbox-landing || true
            rm -rf /tmp/cipherbox-landing || true

      - name: Validate CID
        env:
          # appleboy/ssh-action's capture_stdout appends the drone-ssh banner
          # ("✅ Successfully executed commands to all hosts") to the remote stdout,
          # so outputs.stdout is MULTI-LINE even though the script echoes only the CID.
          # Pass it via env (not inline ${{ }} interpolation) to avoid script injection.
          RAW_STDOUT: ${{ steps.ipfs.outputs.stdout }}
        run: |
          # Extract just the IPFS CID (CIDv0 "Qm…" or CIDv1 "baf…") from the captured
          # output. A bare multi-line value breaks `>> "$GITHUB_ENV"` with
          # "Unable to process file command 'env' … Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'name')".
          CID=$(printf '%s\n' "$RAW_STDOUT" | grep -oE -m1 'Qm[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{44}|baf[a-z2-7]{20,}')
          if [ -z "${CID}" ]; then
            echo "::error::No CID returned from IPFS pin step"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "CID=${CID}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "Pinned landing page to IPFS: ${CID}"

      - name: Update DNSLink
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID }}
          DNSLINK_RECORD_ID: ${{ secrets.DNSLINK_RECORD_ID }}
        run: |
          curl -sS -X PUT \
            "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/${CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID}/dns_records/${DNSLINK_RECORD_ID}" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            --data "{\"type\":\"TXT\",\"name\":\"_dnslink.cipherbox.cc\",\"content\":\"dnslink=/ipfs/${CID}\"}"

          echo "Updated DNSLink to /ipfs/${CID}"

      - name: Summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          {
            echo "## Landing Page Deployed"
            echo "- **CID:** ${CID}"
            echo "- **IPFS Gateway:** https://ipfs.io/ipfs/${CID}"
            echo "- **Commit:** ${{ github.sha }}"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

---
name: project-ssh-host-key-pin-negotiates-rsa-not-ed25519
description: "Pinning a host-key fingerprint for appleboy's ssh/scp actions must match the key Go NEGOTIATES — Ed25519 is last in Go's default order, so a multi-key host serves RSA"
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Ed25519 is LAST in Go's default host-key preference order.** `appleboy/ssh-action` and
`appleboy/scp-action` run `drone-ssh`/`drone-scp` over `easyssh-proxy`, which never sets
`ssh.ClientConfig.HostKeyAlgorithms`. So `x/crypto/ssh`'s `supportedHostKeyAlgos` applies: all the
cert algos, then `rsa-sha2-256`, `rsa-sha2-512`, the three ECDSA curves, and `ssh-ed25519` **last**.

On a host offering ed25519 + rsa + ecdsa (the OpenSSH default), the negotiated key is **RSA**. On
2026-08-06 pinning `vars.SSH_HOST_FINGERPRINT` to the staging box's *ed25519* fingerprint would have
failed all six deploy SSH/SCP steps closed with `ErrFingerprintMismatch` (PR #1114, caught in review
before merge). Reproduce the negotiation before trusting any pin:

```sh
ssh -o HostKeyAlgorithms='rsa-sha2-256,rsa-sha2-512,ecdsa-sha2-nistp256,ecdsa-sha2-nistp384,ecdsa-sha2-nistp521,ssh-ed25519' \
    -v root@HOST exit 2>&1 | grep -i 'Server host key'
```

**The fix was host-side, not a different pin value.** `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-hostkey-ed25519.conf`
on the staging box names `ssh_host_ed25519_key` as the only `HostKey`, so the negotiated key is the
pinned key whatever a client prefers. Pinning the RSA fingerprint instead would work but is brittle:
both actions `curl` the drone binary at run time with **no checksum or signature check**, so the
bundled x/crypto order can change with no diff in this repo. The RSA/ECDSA key files are still on
disk — revert by deleting the drop-in. `sshd -t` before `systemctl reload ssh`; rotating the host key
means updating the variable in the same change.

Two format traps on the value itself:

- The `fingerprint` input **must include the `SHA256:` prefix** — `easyssh-proxy` compares against
  `ssh.FingerprintSHA256(key)`, which returns `"SHA256:" + base64.RawStdEncoding` (unpadded, 43 chars).
- `ssh-keygen -lf -` emits `256 SHA256:… host (ED25519)`. Pasting that whole line sets a value that
  can never match. Use `| cut -d' ' -f2`.

**An empty `fingerprint` makes the action skip verification entirely** — `easyssh-proxy` falls back
to `ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey()`, which accepts any key on every connection (not TOFU: nothing is
pinned even after first sight). So an unset variable fails *open*. Both deploy jobs carry a guard
step matching `SHA256:?*` that fails the job before any SSH step runs.

Pre-existing and still open: the `uses:` SHA pin does not pin the downloaded drone binary.

content.text:
The review caught a blocking defect in my own change — worth stating plainly: **the fingerprint I pinned was the wrong key, and it would have failed every deploy closed.**

`easyssh-proxy` never sets `HostKeyAlgorithms`, so Go's default order applies, and **ed25519 is last in it**. I reproduced it — offering the staging host Go's exact list negotiates `rsa-sha2-256`:

```
debug1: kex: host key algorithm: rsa-sha2-256
debug1: Server host key: ssh-ra SHA256:7sUZ6h…
```

So the client would have compared the RSA key against my ed25519 pin and refused to connect.

**Fixed host-side rather than by swapping the pin value.** `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-hostkey-ed25519.conf` now names `ssh_host_ed25519_key` as the only `HostKey`, so the negotiated key is the pinned key by construction. Verified after reload — Go's order now yields `ssh-ed25519 SHA256:cDyYQQ…`, matching the variable.

I chose that over pinning the RSA fingerprint because both actions `curl` the drone binary at run time with **no checksum check**, so the bundled x/crypto preference order can change with no diff in this repo. Pinning RSA would work today and silently break later. The RSA/ECDSA key files are untouched on disk; reverting is deleting one drop-in.

Also tightened the guard after a second finding: my hint command told operators to run `ssh-keygen -lf -`, whose output is `256 SHA256:… host (ED25519)` — paste that verbatim and an emptiness check accepts a value that can never match. It now matches `SHA256:?*` and hints the command that emits just the token.

#1114 is ready to mark non-draft.

**One thing I did not fix**, flagged for later: the `uses:` SHA pins don't pin the code that opens the connection — both actions download the drone binary at run time unverified. Separate problem, pre-existing.

## Wave 6 is still waiting on you

Nothing has been dispatched. The batch, preconditions and blockers are in my previous message — the short version is that it's launch-ready, and my recommendation is **PRs 1–4 first** (critical path #1109, plus both live bugs), then 5–8 once those are in review, so the review queue doesn't become the bottleneck it was in wave 4.

Two things to decide first: whether to top up macroscope credits (exhausted since yesterday — wave 5's PRs got one bot verdict instead of two, and wave 6 has two XL items plus a crypto tightening), and whether you want all eight in parallel anyway.

### 1. No production caller — the path does not exist

Exhaustive grep across the repo (excluding `target/`, `node_modules/`) for `expand_retire_targets` returns exactly: the definition (`crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs:188`), two `pub use` re-exports (`crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:39`, `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:54`), one doc-link, and six in-module `#[cfg(test)]` call sites. `plan_prune` is the same — it predates this PR and is likewise unwired. So the "expand → `POST /registry/retire`" chain the finding describes is entirely hypothetical composition, not code. That alone puts this under signal-quality criterion 1 (no concrete attack path).

### 2. The exploit premise requires a principal who already holds equivalent destructive power

Write grants are real in v2 (`CONTEXT.md:26,36-39`; `crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs:21`, `accept.rs:632`), so "a foreign writer authors a version record in a scope Alice prunes" is not ruled out by v2.0 scope. That is irrecoverable data loss achievable today, with no bug involved.     self.inner.borrow_mut().child_scopes

**Mechanism:** `child_scopes` is populated verbatim from the root's `write_body.direct_child_scope_index`. That field lives in the write body, sealed under `writeKey = kdf::write_key(kdf::write_seed(writeScopeSeed, scopeId))`. Every **write grantee** holds `writeScopeSeed` (`gate/adoption.rs:613-646` recovers it from the grantee's seed blob), and per `grants/child_index.rs` any write-capable client is *expected* to maintain that index. So the index is attacker-authorable by exactly the principal a `rotateScopeWrite` exists to revoke.

`record_children` skips a child on `scope_id` membership alone. Nothing checks that the skipped id is actually a scope root: not the `ChildScopeRef.ipns_name` (discarded at `:779`), not a grant section, not the owner-signed `GrantSetCommitment`. Contrast the read plane, which resolves every index entry through `RootAdopter` before treating it as a scope root (`net/rotation.rs:474-492`, `:533-539`) — it uses the index to *include* rotation targets; the wave uses it to *exclude*, which is the dangerous direction.

**Impact:** A write grantee, before being revoked, prepends the node ids of ordinary interior folders into `direct_child_scope_index`. The owner's `rotateScopeWrite` then:
- never enumerates those nodes or anything beneath them (`collect_subtree` never queues them),
- leaves their `ChildRef.ipnsName` untouched in the re-sealed parent body (`rewrite_child_names`, `:878-900`: "refs the map does not name keep their names"), so every reader keeps following the old name,
- never retires the old names (`interior_old_names` in `rotate_write.rs:507-525` only covers enumerated nodes).

The revokee keeps `writeSeed(oldWriteScopeSeed, X.id)` → the Ed25519 IPNS keypair and `writeKey` for X and its whole subtree, indefinitely, past a completed rotation. This is a permanent write-revocation bypass, not a wave-bounded forgery window.

**Recommendation:** Anchor the skip on evidence a write grantee cannot forge — the owner-identity-signed commitment.

```rust
// Keep the index entry's own name claim, not just its id.
fn record_child_scopes(&self, index: &[ChildScopeRef]) {
    let mut inner = self.inner.borrow_mut();
    for child in index {
        if let Ok(name) = scope_name(&child.ipns_name) {
            inner.child_scopes.insert(child.scope_id, name);
        }
    }
}

// A child is out of scope only when the parent names it at exactly the
// index's name AND the record there is a scope root whose owner-signed
// commitment binds that name (RootAdopter stages 1-3). Anything else is
// in-scope and must rotate; a resolve failure is fail-closed.
```

Minimum viable hardening if the extra fetch is unacceptable in this slice: require `child.ipns_name == index_entry.ipns_name` for the skip, and treat a mismatch as `ResolveFailure::Rejected`. That alone defeats the planted-id variant, though not an attacker who also rewrites the parent read body.

### [HIGH] The `direct_child_scope_index` skip is unverified — a write grantee can exempt any subtree from every future write rotation

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad37c976fd4198a73/crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:776-781` and `:796`, wired at `:1370-1373`

```rust
fn record_child_scopes(&self, index: &[ChildScopeRef]) {
    self.inner.borrow_mut().child_scopes
        .extend(index.iter().map(|child| child.scope_id));   // ipns_name discarded
}
// ...
for child in children {
    if inner.child_scopes.contains(&child.id) {
        continue;                                            // skipped, unverified
    }
```

**Mechanism:** `child_scopes` is populated verbatim from the root's `write_body.direct_child_scope_index`. That field lives in the write body, sealed under `writeKey = kdf::write_key(kdf::write_seed(writeScopeSeed, scopeId))`. Every **write grantee** holds `writeScopeSeed` (`gate/adoption.rs:613-646` recovers it from the grantee's seed blob), and per `grants/child_index.rs` any write-capable client is *expected* to maintain that index. So the index is attacker-authorable by exactly the principal a `rotateScopeWrite` exists to revoke.

`record_children` skips a child on `scope_id` membership alone. Nothing checks that the skipped id is actually a scope root: not the `ChildScopeRef.ipns_name` (discarded at `:779`), not a grant section, not the owner-signed `GrantSetCommitment`. Contrast the read plane, which resolves every index entry through `RootAdopter` before treating it as a scope root (`net/rotation.rs:474-492`, `:533-539`) — it uses the index to *include* rotation targets; the wave uses it to *exclude*, which is the dangerous direction.

**Impact:** A write grantee, before being revoked, prepends the node ids of ordinary interior folders into `direct_child_scope_index`. The owner's `rotateScopeWrite` then:
- never enumerates those nodes or anything beneath them (`collect_subtree` never queues them),
- leaves their `ChildRef.ipnsName` untouched in the re-sealed parent body (`rewrite_child_names`, `:878-900`: "refs the map does not name keep their names"), so every reader keeps following the old name,
- never retires the old names (`interior_old_names` in `rotate_write.rs:507-525` only covers enumerated nodes).

The revokee keeps `writeSeed(oldWriteScopeSeed, X.id)` → the Ed25519 IPNS keypair and `writeKey` for X and its whole subtree, indefinitely, past a completed rotation. This is a permanent write-revocation bypass, not a wave-bounded forgery window.

**Recommendation:** Anchor the skip on evidence a write grantee cannot forge — the owner-identity-signed commitment.

```rust
// Keep the index entry's own name claim, not just its id.
fn record_child_scopes(&self, index: &[ChildScopeRef]) {
    let mut inner = self.inner.borrow_mut();
    for child in index {
        if let Ok(name) = scope_name(&child.ipns_name) {
            inner.child_scopes.insert(child.scope_id, name);
        }
    }
}

// A child is out of scope only when the parent names it at exactly the
// index's name AND the record there is a scope root whose owner-signed
// commitment binds that name (RootAdopter stages 1-3). Anything else is
// in-scope and must rotate; a resolve failure is fail-closed.
```

Minimum viable hardening if the extra fetch is unacceptable in this slice: require `child.ipns_name == index_entry.ipns_name` for the skip, and treat a mismatch as `ResolveFailure::Rejected`. That alone defeats the planted-id variant, though not an attacker who also rewrites the parent read body.

<result>## Security review — `feat/fuse-ranged-read-and-plaintext-chunk-cache`

Note: the working tree has **uncommitted cosmetic refactors on top of HEAD** (`cache.rs`, `ops.rs`, `fuse_op_core.rs` — a `CacheBudget::of` dedup, a redundant `BTreeMap::get` removal, comment rewording). Nothing substantive differs. All line numbers below are **working tree**. `cargo check -p cipherbox-fuse --tests` is clean.

---

### Findings

**1. MEDIUM — the assembled read buffer is un-zeroized plaintext, and leaves residue on every realloc**
`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:236` (`let mut out = Vec::new();`), `:252`, `:269`, and `take_from` at `:462-469`.

`out` is a plain `Vec<u8>` grown by repeated `extend_from_slice` (once per block). Two concrete leaks:

- **Realloc residue.** Every growth reallocates; the old allocation holding decrypted file bytes is freed **without wiping** and is handed to the next allocation as-is. At CI framing (16-byte blocks) a 4 KiB read does ~8 reallocs; at production framing a multi-block read does several.
- **Error path.** `self.engine.read_stream(...).await?` at `ops.rs:250` propagates on block *N*. `out` already holds *N-1* blocks of plaintext and is dropped un-wiped. This is exactly the case the engine calls out at `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:288-289` — *"Owns already-assembled plaintext until it is handed to the caller: the trust rejects below abandon a partly-filled buffer (AGENTS.md 7)"* — and solves with `Zeroizing` plus the purpose-built `grow_wiping` (`content/mod.rs:197-207`).

The mount is the terminal owner of `out` until it returns it, so rule 7 applies and the repo already has the established pattern one layer down. Amplifier: `size: u32` is never clamped, so `out` accumulates up to `min(size, file_size)` bytes.

Fix: `let mut out = Zeroizing::new(Vec::new());`, grow through the engine's `grow_wiping` shape (or preallocate `min(end - offset, cap)` once so no realloc occurs), and return `Ok(std::mem::take(&mut *out))`.

**2. LOW — `CacheBudget::for_profile` multiplies without an overflow check, so the plaintext ceiling can silently be wrong**
`crates/fuse/src/cache.rs:44-56`: `max_bytes: profile.chunk_size() * blocks`.

`ContentProfile::new(n)` (`crates/engine/src/content/profile.rs:46`) accepts any nonzero `usize`, and `blocks` is unconstrained above. With `overflow-checks` off in release the product wraps: it can land near `usize::MAX`, which erases the ceiling that is the entire purpose of the type, or near zero, which makes the cache silently refuse every block. The `blocks == 0` guard shows the intent to make an unusable budget unrepresentable; overflow is the other half of it. Downstream, `cache.rs:130` (`self.retained + len > max_bytes`) and `:138` (`self.retained += len`) are unchecked adds against that ceiling.

The two shipped consts are const-evaluated, so `PRODUCTION`/`CI` cannot wrap — this is only reachable through the public `for_profile`. Fix: `profile.chunk_size().checked_mul(blocks)?`.

**3. LOW — `unmount()` is on no drop path**
`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:282`. Not a leak: `OperationCore` owns the `Engine`, so dropping the mount drops `ChunkCache` (every `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` wiped) and drops the `Engine`, whose `Drop` (`facade.rs:3249-3254`) clears `streams.open`. But a mount kept alive after the host tears down its kernel connection holds up to `max_bytes` of plaintext and up to *N* engine stream slots indefinitely, and nothing but adapter discipline calls `unmount()`. Suggest a `Drop for OperationCore` that calls it, so the cache.rs header claim ("a mount torn down without one still leaves no plaintext") is structurally true rather than incidentally true.

**4. Informational — nothing binds the mount's `CacheBudget` to `self.engine.profile()`.** `OperationCore::new` (`ops.rs:66`) takes an arbitrary budget. Correctness survives a mismatch (see below), and the working-tree doc edit at `cache.rs:24-27` now says so accurately — but consider deriving the budget from `engine.profile()` inside `new` and taking only a block count.

---

### Checklist items that are clean (mechanisms verified)

**1. Trust boundaries / cache-vs-version — CLEAN, including the stream-id-reuse question.**
- `LiveStreams.next` (`facade.rs:1406`) is a monotonic `u64` incremented only at `facade.rs:2944`. The `RefCell<LiveStreams>` is constructed once (`facade.rs:1557`) and **never reassigned**; `Engine::shut_down` (`facade.rs:1774-1776`) clears `streams.open` only and leaves `next` intact; there is no `stop()`/reset that restores `LiveStreams::default()` outside a unit test. **StreamHandle ids are never reused for an `Engine`'s lifetime**, so a stale cache entry can never surface under a new stream. Belt-and-braces on top: `release_stream` (`ops.rs:315`) calls `forget_stream` on every close, `unmount` drains, and `attach_stream` refuses a closed handle.
- No path serves unverified bytes: everything in the cache came from `read_stream` → `read_pinned_range` (`content/mod.rs:260-325`), which re-asserts `manifest.size == version.size`, CID-verifies each leaf, unseals under the pinned version's key, and rejects a leaf whose plaintext length disagrees with the manifest.

### [HIGH] `convert_invite_claim` cannot tell an invite link from an ordinary grantee — any committed grantee can mint a permanent third-party grant

**Location:** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-ac61fee549ed9b707/crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs:435-457`

**Mechanism (verified):** the only thing that identifies "the link being claimed" is a linear scan of the resolved ledger for a row whose `recipient_identity_pk` equals the mailbox sender:

```rust
let sender = item.sender_identity.to_sec1();
let mut matches = scope.ledger.iter().filter(|e| e.recipient_identity_pk == sender);
let link = matches.next().ok_or(InviteError::LinkNotCommitted)?;
```

`GrantLedgerEntry` (`crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:41-67`) carries **no invite marker** — an invite row and a personal-grant row are byte-identical in shape (that parity is the module's stated design goal), and `expires_at` is optional on both. So an ordinary contact-anchored grantee Alice can:

1. post an `InviteClaim` to the owner's mailbox signed with **her own** identity key (she owns it; the mailbox sender sig verifies),
2. carry any self-signed contact code she likes (contact codes are self-authenticating — anyone can mint one),
3. have her own row matched at line 440, her own tag pass the `recipient_blinded_tag` re-derivation at line 446 (it is genuinely her tag), her own permission read out of the commitment at 451,
4. and get back a fully valid `ConvertedClaim` the owner then signs and publishes.

**Impact:** a revocation-completeness break, not merely a re-share. Alice can already leak her seed out of band, but that copy dies at the next rotation. This path gives her sockpuppet an **owner-signed, committed tag** that is re-wrapped at every future epoch and survives Alice's own revocation — and it appears in the owner's UI as an ordinary claim-derived grantee. Write-permissioned rows convert at `Permission::Write` (line 474), so the sockpuppet inherits write.

- Prove possession against owner-signed material rather than the ledger. The committed entry already carries `pseudonym_pk = Ed25519(kdf::pseudonym_sign(ECDH(ownerEnc, inviteeEnc), scope_id))`, which a fragment holder can derive (it has the enc secret and the owner's enc pub from the URL bundle) and which the owner has signed. Add a `pseudonymSig` field to `InviteClaim` (Ed25519 over det-CBOR `{domain, v, scopeRootName, contactCode, senderIdentityPk}`) and verify it against `commitment.entries[tag].pseudonym_pk`. Then nothing outside the owner's signature is trusted.

A write-grantee (including a **bearer write-link holder**, i.e. an anonymous URL) re-authors the write-body, points a committed row's `recipient_identity_pk` at a key it controls, and claims that row.

That justification is true instantaneously and false over time: the extra tag is a **new committed grant anchored to an attacker-chosen contact**, which survives the write rotation and read rotation that revoke the attacker's own tag. Revocation completeness, not permission level, is the property at stake.

**Recommendation:** same fix as HIGH (bind to the committed `pseudonym_pk`). If the residual is knowingly kept for this slice, rewrite the test comment to state the actual bound — "a write-grantee can plant a grant that outlives its own revocation" — so the next reader does not read it as harmless.

The owner holds the enc secret and could re-derive cheaply — `convert_invite_claim:446` is exactly the check that belongs there.

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs:283-317` (`InviteClaim` carries no nonce/timestamp/id), consumed at `:419-491`

**Mechanism:** the mailbox is explicitly an integrity-untrusted transport with until-acked retention, and the server chooses what to redeliver. A claim is a static, indefinitely-valid, non-expiring authenticated blob. Sequence: holder claims → owner converts and publishes → owner later revokes that grantee's tag → the server re-serves the retained item → `convert_invite_claim` recomputes `newly_granted = true` (line 478, the tag is gone from the ledger) and re-mints the grant. `entry_is_live` (line 458) does not save this: it gates on the *link's* deadline, not the claim's, and that deadline is the write-grantee-mutable field above.

**Recommendation:** put a monotonic `claimId`/`issuedAt` inside the signed claim payload and have the conversion take the owner-local set of already-converted claim ids and revoked tags; refuse a claim whose derived tag is in the revoked set, or whose `issuedAt` is outside a policy window sourced from the sync timing profile. ```rust

**PR-8 is done — #1117** (draft). First of the eight back; seven still running.

Both issues in one diff as required. The shape of the fix is a single `bodies` map entry acting as an exactly-once token — one `takeBody` drops the map entry, the pull deadline, the sink, and any in-flight pull resolver together, so revoke/detach/cancel/pull-answer are safe in any interleaving. That's the right structure for a concurrency bug; it makes double-close unrepresentable rather than guarded against.

For #1097 the recovery signal is `requestPorts()` at script evaluation — a restarted worker fires neither `install` nor `activate`, so that's the only hook available, and it's where the app-shell precache already re-learns. Notably **no timeout was lengthened and no retry added**, which was the explicit wrong-first-move on both issues.

Gates all clean locally: typecheck, lint, test (385 client tests), tracker-refs — all exit 0.

Two things worth your attention:

**It pushed back on a review finding rather than applying it.** Both simplify passes flagged that a worker restarted by a media fetch broadcasts twice; it verified the actual cost (one extra `MessageChannel`, one aborted in-process `open`, no cursor or stream torn down) and found every dedupe formulation would starve a second tab on a narrower ask. Reasoning is recorded in the PR body. That's the correct handling — the suggestion was a symptom report, not a spec.

**One ownership exception:** it touched `packages/client/src/sw/install.ts` (+2 lines) outside its stated scope, because the pipe owns the ports map but the install wiring is what knows "this is a new worker instance" — without it the fix is dead code. It checked no other agent has an open PR on that file. Legitimate, and the kind of thing I wanted surfaced rather than done silently.

**CI caveat:** only 6 checks have run on the tip commit; the other 12 have been queued ~35 minutes behind the parallel wave-6 branches. Eight concurrent branches saturating the runners is the expected cost of launching all eight at once. The first commit's full set passed and commit 2 is a same-package refactor, so I'm not treating this as a red flag — but I'll confirm the full set is green before it merges rather than taking the local results as proof.

Nothing to decide yet. I'll report the rest as they land.

The engine would serve any window in one call; the loop exists to frame the window into cache-aligned blocks, so a hit answers from memory and a miss costs exactly the sealed chunks it covers. Every block is `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`, so zeroization rides `Drop` on every exit path — eviction, re-insert, oversized refusal, release, unmount, and a teardown that never calls `unmount` (v1's only zeroization point was a `destroy()` callback, so a forced unmount left plaintext in RAM).

content.text:
**PR-1 is done — #1118** (draft). That's the critical-path one: it unblocks #1110 → #1111 → #1112 → #648 → the whole deploy chain.

The design call worth surfacing: **the plaintext cache sits above the facade, keyed by engine `StreamHandle`.** Below the facade would put plaintext inside the engine, which the blueprint forbids; and keying by node id would need head-change detection the FS core can't do — that's exactly v1's stale-read bug class. The agent verified `streams.next` is monotonic and never reset (including across `shut_down`) before relying on a handle pinning one immutable version. That reasoning is sound and it's the part I'd have most wanted checked.

Zeroization is structural rather than manual: every cache block is `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`, so wiping rides `Drop` on eviction, re-insert, refusal, release, unmount — **and on a teardown that never calls `unmount`**. v1's only zeroization point was a `destroy()` callback, so a forced unmount left plaintext in RAM. Fixing that was not in the issue.

The `FUSE Op Core` named CI gate landed with it, satisfying testing law 1 — green in 1m1s.

**The review gates earned their keep here.** Security and crypto/privacy independently found the same MEDIUM: the read window was assembled into a plain `Vec<u8>`, so every reallocation freed an allocation still holding decrypted bytes, and `?` on a failed chunk dropped a partly-filled one. The engine already solves this a layer down with `grow_wiping`; the fix reuses it and hands the buffer out via `mem::take` so the caller is terminal owner. Also a LOW: unchecked multiply in `CacheBudget::for_profile` could wrap to a ceiling the mount can't honour, silent in release — now `checked_mul`.

Four findings were verified and **rejected** with reasons in the PR body, including one suggesting an absence-justifying comment that AGENTS.md explicitly rules out.

Two notes:

**Scope was clean** — `crates/fuse` plus the two files the CI-gate obligation required (`ci.yml`, `blueprint/testing.md`). No engine, web, or client files.

**Follow-up #1121 is filed and edged** (`blocked_by #1109`, verified): the test fixture duplicates ~230 lines of the engine's account fixture, because `crates/engine/src/testkit/` was outside its ownership. Correctly deferred rather than reached for.

**Runner saturation is now confirmed across two agents** — the second commit's Rust jobs haven't started in ~25 minutes. Eight branches is more than this repo's CI can absorb at once. It costs wall-clock, not correctness, and I'll verify each PR's full check set before it merges rather than trusting local runs.

Two of eight back. Six still running.

<result>Wave-6 PR-8 is done. Final state below.

## PR

**#1117** — https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1117 — draft, branch `fix/media-pipe-idle-body-and-worker-restart`, 2 commits. Both issues in one diff as required (`Closes #1063`, `Closes #1097`).

Files: `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts`, `packages/client/src/sw/install.ts`, and the three test files for those modules.

## #1063 — idle body ends on a signal, not a deadline

`bodies` now maps a request id to `{ port, controller, pull }`, the controller captured in the stream's `start` (which runs synchronously inside the `ReadableStream` constructor, so the body is registered before `respond` returns). A private `takeBody` drops everything keyed to a request — entry, armed deadline, sink, and the resolver of any in-flight pull — and returns `null` if another path already ended it. That entry is the exactly-once token, so revoke / detach / cancel / pull-answer are safe in any interleaving: no double `close()`, no orphaned pull promise or timer.

Two endings ride it: an unsolicited `cb:media:error` (what `MediaBroker.revoke` posts) now reaches the body directly instead of being dropped, and `detachPort` errors each idle body at once instead of leaving it to a 30 s deadline whose expiry discarded the port under its siblings. An `open` waiting on a dying port also fails with the port, so `respond`'s retry re-brokers immediately.

## #1097 — killed worker reclaimed by a signal

`MediaPipe.requestPorts()` asks every window client to re-broker; `installServiceWorker` calls it at script evaluation — the only signal available, since a restarted worker fires no `install` and no `activate` (the same reason the app-shell precache already re-learns there). No new tab-side production code: `MediaService` already handled `MEDIA_PORT_REQUEST` and `MediaBroker.serve` already calls `close()`, so recovery is idempotent by construction. `requestPorts` returns early while a port is held, so a live worker never broadcasts and a legitimately paused `<video>` is never reclaimed. No per-cursor idle timer; no timeout lengthened or retried.

## Gates — all local, unpiped, re-run after the review-fix commit

`pnpm install` 0 · `pnpm typecheck` 0 · `pnpm lint` 0 · `pnpm test` 0 (385 client tests) · `pnpm lint:tracker-refs` 0

## Review gates

- **/security-review** — no findings. Verified the three guards on the out-of-band error branch, that `open` resolving `null` can't smuggle a head past the status/header/`safeMimeType`/CSP clamps or steer the retry cross-tab, that the broadcast is unreachable from untrusted input, and that no new plaintext is retained. /crypto-privacy-review not required — no crypto or key material in the diff.
- **/simplify** (4 angles) — folded in as commit 2: `pullTimers` merged into the body entry it was co-keyed with (map + `clearPull` deleted); `failBody` replaced a 4×-repeated take-then-error idiom; `pullWindow` dropped two params aliasing fields of the entry it looks up; an extracted one-line helper went back inline; a redundant pre-`await` guard, a twice-used module constant, and several narrating comments removed; the startup call no longer drops a `matchAll` rejection. Net −23 lines in `pipe.ts` vs commit 1.
- **One finding pushed back on** (raised by two agents): a worker restarted by a media fetch broadcasts twice. Verified the cost is one extra `MessageChannel` and one aborted in-process `open` — both asks post back-to-back, so the tab handles them before the worker's `open` arrives; no cursor or engine stream is torn down. Every dedupe formulation needs per-ask scope tracking to avoid starving a second tab on a narrower ask. Reasoning is in the PR body so a reviewer doesn't re-raise it.
- **CodeRabbit skipped** — "Draft detected", and the brief requires leaving it a draft. macroscope not waited on. No Greptile comment.

Each mechanism was mutation-checked before and after the refactor: reverting the out-of-band error routing, the detach-time controller error, or the `requestPorts` broadcast each turns the matching test red. All new tests are in suites the required **Test** gate already runs.

## #1063 — an idle body ends on a signal

`bodies` now maps a request id to `{ port, controller, pull }`, the controller captured in the stream's `start` (which runs synchronously inside the `ReadableStream` constructor, so the body is registered before `respond` returns). A private `takeBody` drops everything keyed to a request — entry, armed deadline, sink, and the resolver of any in-flight pull — and returns `null` if another path already ended it. That map entry is the exactly-once token, so revoke / detach / cancel / pull-answer are safe in any interleaving: no double `close()`, no orphaned pull promise or timer.

`MediaPipe.requestPorts()` asks every window client to re-broker; `installServiceWorker` calls it at script evaluation — the only signal available, since a restarted worker fires no `install` and no `activate` (the same reason the app-shell precache already re-learns there). ## Report

**PR #1115** (draft) — https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1115
Branch `fix/prune-leaf-expansion-and-pinned-units`, 4 commits, 3 files, +323/−19. All changes in `crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs` plus two barrel re-export lines. **No file outside my ownership was edited.**

### What I implemented

**#849 — leaf expansion.** New `expand_retire_targets(version, root_block)` in `crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs`. Returns every leaf CID then the root **last**, because the root block is the only record of its own leaf list — root-first would make the leaves unnameable and charged forever, i.e. the defect made permanent. The walk is one level (`decode_root` already enforces `raw`-codec links, which name nothing further), block-size-capped before it is hashed. **The API needed no change**: `registry.service.ts` `retire` already advisory-locks every path, bulk-deletes via `In(targets)`, and refcounts before unpinning — correct once the client hands it the full set.

**#850 — units.** `size_bytes` → `pinned_bytes`; `ContentVersion::from_plaintext_size(cid, plaintext, profile)` is the explicit conversion, reusing the existing `sealed_total_bytes`. Then bound **at runtime**: the expansion refuses unless the manifest's own leaf count and actual root-block length account for exactly the pinned total the plan quoted.

**#851 — keep-count.** `plan_prune` takes `NonZeroU64`, matching the `RetentionPolicy::KeepLatest(NonZeroU64)` the call site already holds. The enum was already correct and is untouched.

### Gates (all unpiped, exit codes verified)

| Command | Exit |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | 0 |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | 0 |
| `cargo test --workspace` | 0 |
| `cargo test --release --workspace` | 0 |
| `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` | 0 |

No TypeScript changed, so `pnpm typecheck/lint/test` are unaffected — and CI confirms it (`Typecheck`, `Test`, `API Unit`, `OpenAPI Freshness` all report `skipping`). `pnpm lint:tracker-refs` could not run locally (no `node_modules` in the worktree, and I did not symlink one); **CI's `Tracker Refs` gate passed**, and the diff contains no 3+-digit `#NNN`.

### #872 is NOT fully covered — do not close it

This closes #872's entire remaining blocker set (#849/#850/#851; the fourth, #871, is already closed), but **#872's own acceptance goes well beyond them**: the prune op that ends at publish, the `RetireLedger` seam and its conformance kit, the resumable drain, the `retired: 0` done-signal, and the vault-level pending-reclaim figure with mode-derived legs. The PR body says so explicitly and uses `Part of #872`, not `Closes`.

Worth flagging: the maintainer's own audit comments on all three recommend closing them as *folded into* #872 rather than shipping separately, since `plan_prune` has zero production callers. I shipped them because they were assigned, they are real, and they land in exactly the shapes #872 specified — but the fix is **inert at runtime** until #872 wires a caller.

### Review gates — findings and resolution

All three ran on `git diff main...HEAD`. Folded in: routing the address check through core's `decode_content_cid_str` + `is_plane_anchor` + `verify_cid` instead of a bespoke multibase string compare (so the failure carries core's already-KAT-pinned `TrustViolation::ContentCidMismatch`, and an off-plane root CID is refused as malformed rather than conflated with substitution); binding the drain-time byte total to the plan, which collapsed a whole `RetireExpansion` struct away; deleting an absence-justifying comment about recursion the function does not do, an invariant restated on four sites, and a doc claim that a constructor was "the only way to build" a struct with public fields; a redundant test folded into its neighbour; `with_capacity` over a `collect`-then-`push` realloc.

Two findings I **did not** apply literally, filed instead with native `blocked_by` edges to #872 (verified bidirectional, keyed by database id), both `v2-build` / `comp:engine` / milestone v2.0.0:

- **#1124** — the expansion cannot subtract a leaf a *retained* version also references. Not reachable for honest versions (fresh per-version key + per-chunk nonce make leaf sets disjoint) but adversarially reachable via a write-grantee. The reviewer's proposed `retained: &BTreeSet` parameter is speculative ahead of the caller that knows the retained set, and it breaks the closed-form byte accounting.
- **#1125** — `registry_cids` in `sync/drain.rs` derives the same CID set for the register/abandon path with the *opposite* ordering. I verified both are correct for their own path (the expansion key differs: staging there, the root block here), but nothing holds the two sets equal. Unifying needs the prune drain, and `sync/` was another agent's this wave.

### Deliberately out of scope

The retire ledger and drain (#872's own scope); any `apps/api/src/registry/` change (verified unnecessary); adding `ExpandError` to the `kat_content.rs` reject-vector surface — routing through core's `TrustViolation` gave the trust check a pinned home without editing that shared file.

PR is left as a **draft**; CodeRabbit correctly reports `Review skipped: draft pull request` and has not been triggered.</result>

content.content:
Recommendation: close as folded into #872 once #872 ships.

Audit against `main` @ `3d087d673`, 2026-08-06.

The analysis here is correct, but the defect is latent — it is documented, not reachable. `plan_prune` has zero production callers. Every reference is a re-export or its own unit test:

- Re-exports: `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:54`, `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:38`.
- Callers: `crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs:175`, `:187`, `:189` — all inside the module's own `#[cfg(test)]` block.

The retire leg is the same story: `ApiClient::retire` is exercised only from `crates/contract/tests/contract.rs`. No production path plans a prune or hands targets to retire, so no account is being charged for orphaned leaves today.

That makes this a design constraint on the prune slice rather than a bug to fix on `main`. #872 already carries it as a scoped prerequisite, including the two shape constraints (`root + leaf_cids` cannot be one call at `MAX_BATCH = 1000`; leaves retire before their root) and the ledger-stores-roots decision that depends on this expansion.

Recommend closing this as folded into #872 when #872 ships. Fixing the DAG expansion separately would mean shipping an expansion with no caller, and #872 would immediately reshape it around the retire ledger.

        Err(GateError::Rejected(rejection)) => {

/// Gate a scope root's record, recovering this pass's own read at the durable
/// sequence floor ([`reread_at_floor`]).
async fn gated_scope_root<H: Http, F: FloorStore>(
    adopter: RootAdopter<'_, H, F>,
    name: &IpnsName,
    record_bytes: &[u8],
) -> Result<GatedScopeRoot, ResolveFailure> {
    match adopter.adopt_root(name, record_bytes).await {
        Ok((candidate, outcome)) => Ok(GatedScopeRoot {
            envelope: candidate.envelope,
            section: candidate.grant_section,
            read_body: outcome.adopted.read_body,
            read_scope_seed: outcome.read_scope_seed.ok_or(ResolveFailure::Unavailable)?,
            write_scope_seed: outcome.write_scope_seed,
        }),
        Err(GateError::Seam(_)) => Err(ResolveFailure::Unavailable),
        Err(GateError::Rejected(rejection)) => {
            reread_at_floor(&adopter, name, record_bytes, &rejection.reason).await
        }
    }
}
```

- B (`:1042-1061`): `let gated = gated_scope_root(adopter, name, record_bytes).await.map_err(wave_read_verdict)?;` — and with finding 2 applied, just `.await?`
- C (`:1129-1137`): `let envelope = gated_scope_root(adopter, &name, &record_bytes).await?.envelope;`

<result>## Task A — test fixture duplication

### A1. `staged_root_naming` is a helper three EXISTING tests already need (top value)
`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:3586-3602` builds an `OwnerRootSpec` whose every field but `children` is fixed, then stages it. That exact literal + `harness.stage(SCOPE, &root, Some(OWNER_ROOT_EPOCH))` pair already appears verbatim **three times** in the pre-existing wave tests:

- `3222-3232` (`a_read_only_holder_descends_the_whole_subtree_after_the_wave`) — `children: vec![ref_to(mid_id, &mid_old)]`
- `3272-3282` (`a_moved_root_re_signs_its_commitment_over_the_new_name`) — `children: vec![ref_to(leaf_id, &leaf_old)]`
- `3351-3361` (`a_failed_root_publish_leaves_the_root_republishable`) — `children: Vec::new()`

All three carry `scope_id: SCOPE, root_id: SCOPE, child_scope_index: Vec::new(), parent_node_seed: None, owner_write_blob_epoch: Some(OWNER_ROOT_EPOCH)` and are followed by the same `harness.stage`. So `staged_root_naming` is the right helper — it just needs to be **hoisted above them and adopted**, not left at the bottom serving only the new tests. That's ~33 lines removed, and the helper stops looking like a fifth copy.

It also near-duplicates the module's own `scope_root` at `1603-1618`, which is the identical `OwnerRootSpec` literal with `children: Vec::new()` hard-coded and index/ascent-seed parameterized. Concrete shape:

```rust
fn scope_root(
    scope_id: [u8; 16],
    children: Vec<ChildRef>,                    // new param
    child_scope_index: Vec<ChildScopeRef>,
    parent_node_seed: Option<[u8; 32]>,
) -> OwnerRootFixture
```
`vault_root`/`interior` pass `Vec::new()`; `staged_root_naming` becomes three lines over it. One `OwnerRootSpec` literal survives in the whole test module instead of six.

### A2. `staged_scope_with_index` should be built on `staged_root_naming`
`3557-3577` writes the `OwnerRootSpec` literal a sixth time. The only delta from `staged_root_naming` is `child_scope_index`. Give `staged_root_naming` an index parameter (or add a `_with_index` sibling) and the fixture collapses to:

```rust
let root = staged_root_naming_with_index(
    harness,
    vec![ref_to(MID, &mid_old), ref_to(CHILD_SCOPE, &descendant.name)],
    index(&descendant),
);
```

### A3. `mid_name()` is redundant *and* misplaced
`3696-3699`:
```rust
fn mid_name() -> IpnsName {
    derive_write_name(&OWNER_ROOT_WRITE_SCOPE_SEED, &MID)
}
```
It sits **between two `#[test]` fns** (`a_planted_index_entry_…` at 3666 and `a_node_no_gated_record_named…` at 3701) — fixtures in this module are grouped at 3551-3630, so at minimum it belongs there. But it should disappear entirely: it is exactly the `mid_old` that `staged_scope_with_index` already computes at `3562` and returns. Its two uses are both inside one test (`3679` building the planted `ChildScopeRef`, and `3684`'s `assert_eq!(mid_old, mid_name())` — a pure fixture self-check that exists only because the closure can't see `mid_old`).

- `2932-2939` — inside `published_head`, fetch + unmarshal + verify
- `3460-3466` and `3476-3482` — `the_canonical_repoint_lands_on_the_scope_pointer_record`, the identical 7-line fetch/unmarshal/verify block twice in one test
- `3839-3844` — the new `the_production_edges_carry_the_whole_wave…`, the same thing again

One helper serves all five:
```rust
fn verified_at<T: RecordTransport + Clone>(h: &Harness<T>, name: &IpnsName) -> Option<VerifiedRecord> {
    let bytes = h.store.record_at(&h.store.endpoints()[0], name.as_str())?;
    IpnsRecord::unmarshal(&bytes).and_then(|r| r.verify(name)).ok()
}
```
`published_at` becomes `verified_at(..).is_some()` at its two call sites (`3745`, `3752`, `3785`) — or is dropped for an inline `.is_none()` assert. Net ~25 lines, and the pointer test stops repeating itself.

### A5. `staged_scope` should return the descendant it staged
`3877` inside `the_production_edges_carry_the_whole_wave_from_enumeration_to_re_point`:
```rust

```
`staged_scope_with_index` already built exactly this at `3563` and threw it away. Return it (3-tuple, or a small `StagedScope { root, mid_old, descendant }` — the tuple is already at two elements and the third would be past the readable limit, so the struct is the better shape). The test then asserts against the fixture it was actually staged from rather than a re-derivation that silently drifts if `interior`'s inputs change.

`3606-3622` duplicates `crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate_write.rs:924-943` (`fn plan`), differing only in the constant values. Both live in private `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, so sharing means promoting one to `testkit`. Not worth it for two call sites — noting only so it isn't a third time.

### A7. The new test comment restates the production doc comment verbatim
`3667-3671`:
> `directChildScopeIndex` is authored by any committed writer, including the grantee this rotation cuts. An entry naming an ordinary in-scope node would carve it out of the wave and leave it live at a name the revokee's retired write scope seed still derives…

is the same rationale as `1101-1107` on `record_scope_boundary`, nearly word for word. AGENTS.md: state it once at its home. The test comment should shrink to one line naming the behaviour under test; the test name already carries most of it.

---

## Task B — production-code efficiency / wasted work

### B1. Every interior node is fetched, gated, and unsealed TWICE per wave (biggest item)
`rotate_scope_write` runs `collect_subtree` (`rotation/rotate_write.rs:664-698`) as a **complete BFS pass** before any republish. So:

- Pass 1, `resolve_node` (`net/rotation.rs:1408`): `fanout_get_verify` at the old name → `interior_source` → `ChildAdopter::adopt` (gateway head-block fetch + unseal) → `open_carried_at_floor` (second unseal off the cached candidate). Everything but `child_node_ids` is then **dropped on the floor** — the `WaveSource` is parked only for the root (`1429-1431`).
- Pass 2, `republish` (`1452-1467`): `gated_root.take()` misses for every interior node, so it does `fanout_get_verify` again → constructs a **fresh** `ChildAdopter` (`983`), whose `assembled` cache is empty → gateway head-block fetch again → adopt (now floor-rejected) → `open_carried_at_floor` again.
- Plus `republish_node` calls `is_republished` (`rotate_write.rs:625`), a third fan-out GET at the new name.

Per interior node per wave: **3 record fan-out GETs, 2 gateway block fetches, 4 unseals** where 2/1/2 would do. `GatedWaveRoot` is exactly the mechanism that already fixes this for one node; widening it to `BTreeMap<IpnsName, WaveSource>` (or folding it into `WaveSubtree`, see B2's sibling note) halves the network cost of the whole wave.

Tradeoff to state, not hide: that holds every node's `ReadBody` in memory for the duration of the wave. `WaveSubtree` is already O(subtree) (`764`, a name per node), so the *count* is not new, only the per-entry size. If the parking is deliberately root-only for memory reasons, `GatedWaveRoot`'s doc (`815-823`) explains only the *correctness* reason and should say so — as written a reader concludes interior re-reads are an oversight.

### B2. `record_scope_boundary` is the third copy of the adopt-or-recover prologue

| | fan-out GET | `RootAdopter::new` + ascent seed | `adopt_root` → `Ok` / `Seam` / `Rejected`→`reread_at_floor` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OwnerRotationNet::gated_root` `406-438` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `WriteWaveNet::root_source` `1030-1061` | (caller) | ✓ | ✓ |
| `WriteWaveNet::record_scope_boundary` `1114-1137` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

The match arms are the duplicated core. Extract a free fn next to `reread_at_floor`:

```rust
async fn adopt_or_recover<H: Http, F: FloorStore>(
    adopter: &RootAdopter<'_, H, F>,
    name: &IpnsName,
    record_bytes: &[u8],
) -> Result<GatedScopeRoot, ResolveFailure>
```

Then `gated_root`'s tail is one line, `root_source:1045-1061` becomes `adopt_or_recover(&adopter, name, record_bytes).await.map_err(wave_read_verdict)?`, and `record_scope_boundary:1129-1137` becomes `adopt_or_recover(&adopter, &name, &record_bytes).await?.envelope`. ~45 lines → ~18, and the three sites can no longer drift on which rejections recover.

One behaviour caveat to decide explicitly rather than absorb silently: today `record_scope_boundary`'s `Ok` arm reads only `candidate.envelope` and ignores `outcome.read_scope_seed`, so a **keyless** descendant scope root still proves the boundary; the shared helper's `read_scope_seed.ok_or(Unavailable)` would turn that into a stall. `gated_root` already treats keyless as `Unavailable` (see the existing test `a_root_held_keyless_yields_no_index_and_no_rejection`, `1980`), so unifying is defensible — but it is a change, not a refactor, and should land with a test.

Related: `record_scope_boundary` re-derives `kdf::node_seed(read_scope_seed, &child.scope_id)` per entry (`1119`), which is exactly what `RotationAncestry::parent_node_seed` (`246-258`) memoizes for the read-plane net. Two nets, two mechanisms for the same derivation — worth a note even if unifying is out of scope here.

### B3. `resolve_node` round-trips its own error type
`1411-1417` calls `root_source`/`interior_source`, which produce `WritePublishError`, then converts back with `subtree_verdict` (`924-931`, new in this diff). **PR-7 is done — #1122** (draft, 21 files, all CI green). Zero file overlap with the other three finished PRs — I checked all four sets pairwise.

**#1091** holds selection as hex node-id keys and derives the selected *rows* from the live listing, so a row the engine retires leaves the selection with it. That sidesteps the known web/SDK folder-state desync class entirely rather than patching around it — no manual prune, no client-side listing patching. Batch move/delete dispatch one facade command per node under a single busy/error envelope, so every node is attempted and the first refusal surfaces.

**#1087** was the more interesting fix. It bounds the mount-time restore with a 10 s deadline and reports `'checking' | 'ready' | 'unavailable'` — **silence past the deadline is a verdict**, which is what makes the never-resolves case terminate rather than hang. A late-landing restore still promotes back to `ready`, so the tab self-heals instead of being stuck on a pessimistic answer.

It also **restored a weakened smoke assertion to its unconditional form** — that test had been softened to accommodate the bug. Worth knowing that had happened.

Runtime-verified with Puppeteer against a live stack: deep-link redirect with the reason shown, batch move excluding the selected folder from its own destination list, row-menu delete on one of two selected rows leaving the other selected. Screenshots at each step.

**Pushed back on two review findings with measurement**, which is the right instinct: it applied the "replace the spacer span with CSS padding" suggestion, measured it mis-aligning the `[..]` row by exactly the flex `gap`, and reverted it.

**Scope caveat:** it edited beyond its literal file list — the file-browser components, dialogs, `useFolderPicker`, and the web-e2e page object. #1091 isn't implementable without the list components, and I'd written `apps/web/src/.../SelectionActionBar.tsx` with an ellipsis, which it read as covering the file-browser surface. Fair reading, and no collision resulted. It stayed clear of the client SW files PR-8 owns.

Follow-up **#1126** filed and edged: bounding the live stream-ticket set a large batch download can open.

Four of eight back — PRs 1, 5, 7, 8. Still running: **2** (`WriteSubtreeResolver`), **3** (adoption-gate DoS), **4** (write clobber), **6** (grant invites) — the four engine-heavy ones.

The PR-5 question is still open: merge #1115 as groundwork, or fold #849/#850/#851 into #872 per your own audit.

Both review gates independently found the **same HIGH** in my first draft: it located the invite row by scanning the resolved ledger for the mailbox sender's `recipientIdentityPk`. Nothing in a published record marks a row as an invite — that byte-shape parity is the design — and the fields that could sit outside the owner's signature. So **any committed grantee** could post an honestly-signed claim naming a sockpuppet contact and have its own row convert; a write-grantee reached the same sink by re-authoring that field on someone else's row. `mint_invite_grant` now returns `MintedInvite`, and conversion/revocation take a `RecordedInvite` — so the `CreateInviteLink` facade arm **must persist that record**. It's the thing that makes claims safe. Whoever picks up #1016 needs that.
